Its platform ingests, curates and animates clinical trial data through products including the Data Hub, Smart Data Quality (SDQ), Operational Insights, Patient Insights, Source to Submission (S2S) and the BRAIN family (BRAIN SDTM, BRAIN SCE, BRAIN Visualization, BRAIN Consortium), alongside a set of modular Clinical AI Agents announced in 2025. Saama states its platform offers 40-plus pre-built connectors and that its agents are "connected via APIs", but as of this profile the company publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification - technical documentation and the support portal both sit behind a customer login.

providers.name: Waiv
providers.description: Waiv is a Paris-based AI precision-testing company spun out of Owkin (formerly Owkin Dx) that builds clinically validated, AI-powered diagnostic tests for oncology and digital pathology. Its products — RlapsRisk BC (breast-cancer distant-relapse risk), the MSIntuit Suite (MSI/dMMR pre-screening in colorectal, gastric and endometrial cancer), BRCAura RUO (gBRCA pre-screening) and TLS Detect — read routine H&E whole-slide images to accelerate biomarker detection, outcome prediction and treatment-response assessment. The tests are delivered through Destra, an AI-native digital pathology platform that lab and clinician users reach in the browser and that laboratories can wire into an existing IMS/LIS through the Destra API. RlapsRisk BC and MSIntuit CRC hold dual CE-IVD marking under the EU IVDR. Waiv raised $33M led by OTB Ventures and Alpha Intelligence Capital, with Serena, Karista and SistaFund participating, and later closed $35M total with CRB Health Tech. The Destra API is advertised on the product page but is sales-gated — there is no public developer portal, reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Champ Ai
providers.description: Champ AI is an AI operations platform that automates complex, multi-step enterprise back-office workflows through autonomous agents that browse, read, call, and act on behalf of operations teams. Positioned as an AI-native replacement for traditional business process outsourcing (BPO), Champ combines browser automation across legacy portals and internal tools, document intelligence, outbound voice AI, and SOP-to-agent conversion with process mining and more than 100 integrations. The platform targets regulated, operations-heavy verticals such as healthcare and professional employer organizations (PEO), claiming 95%+ accuracy on complex standard operating procedures and 4-10x ROI on operational spend. Founded by Jagannath Putrevu, Ted Cheng, and Peter Lin (early Instacart operators), Champ AI emerged from stealth in May 2026 with an $8.5M seed round led by Redpoint Ventures with participation from defy.vc and SV Angel. This profile was surfaced as a Redpoint Ventures portfolio company and enriched from the company's public website; Champ AI does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Forus
providers.description: Forus (formerly Tandem) is an AI-powered healthcare technology company operating a network that connects physicians, pharmacies, payers, and biopharmaceutical companies to accelerate patient access to prescribed medicines. Its platform automates the administrative work between a clinical decision and treatment initiation: insurance prior authorization, AI-generated denial appeals, financial-assistance enrollment, benefit verification, and pharmacy fulfillment routing. Forus is embedded in physician workflows across most U.S. zip codes and is SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant. It offers no public developer API, OpenAPI spec, or SDKs; this profile captures the company's public web, trust, and security surface.

providers.name: HealthJoy
providers.description: HealthJoy is a Chicago-based employee-benefits engagement, healthcare navigation, and cost-containment platform founded in 2014, which markets itself as a "Benefits Operating System" (BOS) for employers and benefit consultants. It unifies fragmented health benefits into a single member-facing app combining Joy AI — a 24/7 AI assistant trained on each client's benefits plan — with a licensed human healthcare concierge team, provider search with cost scores and quality ratings, prescription savings, medical bill review, and an intelligent steerage engine that routes members to high-value, fair-priced care. Employers and consultants get a client dashboard reporting engagement, utilization, savings, and ROI. HealthJoy reports 1,800+ client companies and 1.25M+ members. It publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract; integrations with benefits-administration and TPA vendors (e.g. Employee Navigator) are delivered as managed eligibility/census data feeds set up by its implementation team rather than as a self-serve API.

providers.name: Arine
providers.description: Arine is a San Francisco-based healthcare technology company that operates an AI-driven medication intelligence and comprehensive medication management platform for health plans, government payors and risk-bearing provider organizations. The platform ingests pharmacy and medical claims, clinical, cost, quality, behavioral and social-determinants-of-health data, then applies machine learning and clinical decision logic to surface medication-related gaps in care and generate targeted, just-in-time interventions, member education materials and prescriber communications. Arine packages this as four solutions — LUMINATE (high-risk member management), RESONATE (prescriber analytics), ELEVATE (Star Ratings and quality improvement) and ELEVATE MTM (medication therapy management) — delivered as a SaaS portal running in AWS. The Arine Platform holds HITRUST Risk-based 2-year (r2) certification. Arine ships no public developer program: its API gateway at api.arine.io is closed to anonymous callers and its product documentation portal at docs.arine.io sits behind customer authentication, so no machine-readable API contract is publicly available.

providers.name: Clipboard Health
providers.description: Clipboard Health (now branded simply "Clipboard", at clipboardworks.com) is a U.S. healthcare workforce marketplace that connects workplaces — long-term care facilities, home health and hospice agencies, hospitals, dental practices, and travel assignments — with vetted, independent professionals to fill open shifts. Workplaces post shifts and Clipboard matches, credentials, schedules, and pays qualified workers, with the platform handling documentation, compliance, and instant pay for pros. The company reports serving more than 6,500 workplaces and over a million workers nationwide. Backed by Initialized Capital and IVP, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. Clipboard Health publishes no public consumer API; its public developer surface is limited to open-source TypeScript utility libraries on npm (the @clipboard-health scope, from github.com/ClipboardHealth/core-utils) and a minimal RFC 9116 security.txt.

providers.name: GSK
providers.description: GSK plc (formerly GlaxoSmithKline, rebranded in May 2022) is a global biopharma headquartered in the United Kingdom and dual-listed on the London Stock Exchange and NYSE under the ticker GSK. Following the July 2022 spin-off of its consumer-health business as Haleon, GSK is now a focused biopharma operating across four therapeutic areas — infectious diseases, HIV, oncology, and respiratory/immunology/inflammation — with flagship vaccine franchises including Shingrix and Arexvy and an HIV joint venture (ViiV Healthcare) held with Pfizer and Shionogi. GSK does not publish a public developer portal or commercial REST APIs. Machine-readable surfaces are limited to press, podcast and investor RSS feeds, the GSK Study Register and the ClinicalStudyDataRequest (CSDR) consortium portal for patient-level clinical trial data, registrations on ClinicalTrials.gov, and R/Python tooling published by the GSK-Biostatistics GitHub organization.

providers.name: Lighten
providers.description: Lighten Platforms, Inc. is a San Mateo, California healthcare AI company building an AI-native platform for clinical evidence curation from electronic health record (EHR) data. Its 360° EHR Curation Platform reasons over unstructured clinical notes together with structured records to reconstruct complete patient journeys, applying clinically validated quality assurance at the variable, patient, and cohort level rather than relying on model accuracy metrics alone. On top of that curation layer Lighten delivers Apps & Insights for patient finding and HCP targeting, longitudinal patient journeys, and market intelligence, plus a "Beyond Claims" offering that integrates curated EHR signal with claims data for broader coverage. The company serves life sciences, health systems, data and analytics consultancies, and investors, and was founded by Xinkun Nie, PhD. Lighten publishes no public developer API program, SDKs, or developer documentation as of this profile.

providers.name: Loa Healthcare Pricing API
providers.description: Source-labeled U.S. healthcare price transparency API and MCP server. Provides hospital and provider entity search, source-labeled price rows, cross-entity price comparison by CPT/HCPCS, and a reviewed update-submission workflow. Data comes from 6,000+ hospital Machine Readable Files under the federal Hospital Price Transparency Rule plus CMS NPI Registry and Loa-reviewed provider submissions.

providers.name: Rite Aid
providers.description: Rite Aid is one of the nation's leading drugstore chains, providing prescription drugs, health and beauty aids, and convenience items. Rite Aid supports vendor integrations through EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) and B2B services, and offers digital health tools including an AI health assistant, pharmacy services, vaccination record management, and preventive health screening programs.

providers.name: Camber
providers.description: Camber is a healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM) and medical billing software platform purpose-built for specialty care providers, including ABA (applied behavior analysis) therapy, physical therapy, and ENT and allergy clinics. The platform automates the full claims lifecycle — creation and submission, pre-submission scrubbing and eligibility verification, payment posting and reconciliation, and denial management and prevention — using a rules engine and AI trained on billions of dollars in real claims data, combined with human review where judgment matters. Founded in 2021 (Y Combinator W21, rebranded from Juniper Behavioral Health to Camber), the New York-based company is backed by Craft Ventures, a16z, and Y Combinator, and processes over a million claims annually for hundreds of specialty care providers across all 50 states.

providers.name: Carepatron
providers.description: Carepatron is a cloud-based healthcare practice management and EHR platform for therapists, counselors, psychologists, health coaches, nutritionists, and other practitioners. It brings client records, appointment scheduling and online booking, telehealth, AI-assisted clinical notes and documentation, and billing/invoicing with insurance claims into one workspace, and markets HIPAA/SOC/GDPR compliance across 100,000+ clinicians in 120+ countries. As of this review Carepatron does NOT publish a documented public developer API - its pricing page lists "API (coming soon)" on the Advanced plan, and there is no developer portal, API reference, published base URL, OpenAPI definition, or SDK. Third-party connectivity today is limited to a handful of native integrations (Zoom, accounting software, Google Tag Manager). The APIs listed below are logical/product-area groupings modeled from Carepatron's own feature set; their endpoints are NOT documented and are marked as modeled, not confirmed.

providers.name: Clara 2
providers.description: Clara is an AI-powered primary care and longevity practice, founded by the team behind Circle Medical and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026) and A.Capital. Clara pairs deep clinical AI with board-certified clinician review: it securely imports and analyzes a patient's medical records, surfaces health trends, assists with symptom assessment, medication refills, lab ordering, and longevity/biomarker goals, and routes every medical recommendation to a licensed clinician for review and approval before it reaches the patient. The company operates as a fully licensed primary care practice across all 50 U.S. states and is a HIPAA-covered entity. Clara is a consumer telehealth product (subscription plans on askclara.com) and currently publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity, trust, and compliance surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Granted
providers.description: Granted is an AI-plus-human healthcare navigation service that helps consumers reduce medical bills and manage health insurance. The platform detects billing errors (duplicate line items, up-coding, incorrect charges), finds unadvertised financial-assistance programs, negotiates discounts, optimizes insurance benefits, and manages claims communication across more than 1,300 insurance companies and patient portals. It runs on a success-based model that is free to use, charging only when it saves the user money (capped at $300 per bill or 10% of savings). Granted is a Forerunner Ventures portfolio company operating in the consumer health / medical-billing sector. It publishes a consumer web and iOS app rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Lecturio
providers.description: Lecturio is a medical and nursing education technology company headquartered in Leipzig, Germany (Lecturio GmbH), serving more than 500,000 learners and educators across 175+ countries. The platform combines video lectures, concept pages, spaced-repetition quizzes, and AI-tutored question banks covering 20+ preclinical and clinical subjects, with exam preparation for USMLE, NBME, COMLEX, MCAT, PANCE, NCLEX-RN, and international licensure exams such as the Saudi SNLE. Alongside the direct-to-student Lecturio Medical and Lecturio Nursing products, the company sells institutional platforms to medical schools, nursing schools, hospitals, and residency programs under the Healer (clinical reasoning), SimTutor (simulation authoring), and SIMTICS (procedural simulation) brands. Lecturio publishes no public developer API or developer portal; its public machine-readable surface consists of an RFC 9116 security.txt, a self-managed vulnerability disclosure policy, and a Rank Math generated llms.txt.

providers.name: Mabel
providers.description: Mabel is a healthcare technology company (Irvine, California; backed by 500 Global) that helps Medicare accountable care organizations (ACOs) enroll and engage beneficiaries. Its platform is a market leader in voluntary alignment, used by roughly one in three ACOs, and spans four core solutions: Voluntary Alignment (campaign execution, response processing, analytics, and compliance auditing for LEAD, ACO REACH, and GUIDE programs), Health Surveys (social determinants of health screenings, NPS, and custom surveys with CMS-formatted reporting), Beneficiary Notifications (compliance notices via email, mail, or SMS with audit-ready tracking), and Letters From Your Doctor (provider-based outreach for enrollment, surveys, and appointments). Mabel is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified. No public developer API or SDK surface is published at this time; this profile captures the company's identity, compliance posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: OWKIN
providers.description: Owkin is a French-American AI-biotech company (offices in New York, Paris, and London) that builds K Pro, an agentic "AI biology" platform for pharmaceutical and biotech R&D. K Pro pairs large-language-model agents with Owkin's multimodal patient-data network — spanning 164 academic institutions, the MOSAIC spatial-omics dataset, and public sources such as TCGA and PubMed — to help scientists identify drug targets, prioritize indications, explore cohorts, review literature, and navigate clinical trials. Owkin is also known for open-source federated-learning and computational- pathology research (FLamby, PyDESeq2, HistoSSLscaling). The company is backed by GV (Google Ventures). Owkin exposes product documentation and an agentic app (K Pro) but no public developer/REST API.

providers.name: Rivet Health
providers.description: Rivet Health is a cloud-based revenue cycle management (RCM) platform for healthcare providers, spanning practices, specialty groups, and hospitals. Its software brings together three core modules: Revenue Diagnostics (AI-driven revenue forecasting, real-time reporting, and denial prevention), Payer Performance (contract management, payer benchmarking, and fee-schedule administration), and Patient Pricing (automated patient cost estimates and No Surprises Act Good Faith Estimates). Rivet describes itself as an agnostic platform that integrates with 30+ practice-management systems, EHRs, and clearinghouses — including Epic, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, AdvancedMD, Veradigm, ModMed, Greenway Health, Nextech, Availity, and Change Healthcare. The company is backed by Menlo Ventures. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API reference documentation; integrations are delivered through its partner network. Rivet publishes a trust center documenting SOC 2 and HIPAA posture.

providers.name: Spectrum Medical
providers.description: Spectrum Medical is a privately held medical technology company, co-founded by Steve Turner and Mark Drain, with corporate headquarters in Cheltenham, England, a U.S. headquarters in Fort Mill, South Carolina, and a European headquarters in Mirandola, Italy. It entered the global medical device market in 2005 with its non-invasive System M diagnostic technology and today builds two connected product families: Quantum Perfusion Technologies (workstations, centrifugal and roller pumps, oxygenators, heater-coolers, sensor modules and single-use sterile technologies for cardiopulmonary bypass, ECMO and other extracorporeal therapies) and Quantum Informatics (the VIPER clinical interfacing EMR, the VISION server and Perfusion Information Management System). Its software surface is a customer-deployed, on-premise stack: the VISION server passes case data to the hospital EHR over HL7 v2 interfaces through a bundled Mirth Connect interface engine, and third-party device connectivity is delivered through optional device-driver software rather than a public web API. Spectrum Medical is ISO/IEC 27001:2013 certified and its VIPER Clinical Information Solution 3.0 earned ONC-HIT 2014 Edition Modular Certification via the Drummond Group. Systems are in use in over 60 countries.

providers.name: Basata
providers.description: Basata is a Phoenix-based healthcare AI company building the operational layer for American medical practices. Its AI agents automate back-office administrative work — processing patient referrals, answering phone calls 24/7, and managing faxes and patient communications — while integrating with existing EHR systems so clinical staff can focus on patient care instead of paperwork. Founded in 2024 by Kaled Alhanafi (CEO, formerly Lyft and Cruise), Chetan Patel (co-founder and president, formerly Medtronic), and Vivin Paliath (co-founder and CTO), Basata raised a $21M Series A led by Basis Set Ventures with Cowboy Ventures and PHX Ventures participating (~$24.5M total). The platform is marketed as fully HIPAA-compliant and the company publishes a SOC 2 attestation. Basata does not currently expose a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity and web properties.

providers.name: RapidClaims
providers.description: RapidClaims is a healthcare revenue-cycle-management (RCM) company building autonomous AI agents for medical coding and claims. Its platform automates medical coding (RapidCode), value-based-care coding and risk adjustment (RapidVBC), denial management and revenue recovery (RapidRecovery), and a unified revenue cycle platform (RapidRCM) for FQHCs, community health centers, ACOs, physician groups, ambulatory surgery centers, hospitals, and management services organizations. The company emphasizes a healthcare-grade security and compliance posture (HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2 Type II, 256-bit encryption). RapidClaims is backed by Accel and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Afilio
providers.description: Afilio (Afilio - Gesellschaft für Vorsorge mbH) is a Berlin-based digital provision platform ("Vorsorgeplattform") that helps German families prepare for emergencies, care situations, and death. Through a paid membership, users create legally valid advance directives (Patientenverfügung), healthcare powers of attorney (Vorsorgevollmacht), and wills (Testament), and maintain a digital inventory of documents and assets. A central emergency card gives doctors and relatives 24/7 access to critical medical and provision information, and Afilio also assists with care-level (Pflegegrad) applications and expert consultation. Over four million families use the GDPR-compliant service. Afilio is a consumer (B2C) platform and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public product, legal, and security surface. Backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: Lively
providers.description: Lively is a fintech-healthtech company that provides modern, cloud-based Health Savings Accounts (HSA) alongside Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA), Health Reimbursement Arrangements (HRA), COBRA, and commuter benefits for individuals, families, employers, benefits administrators, and third-party administrators. Lively pairs interest-bearing and investment-enabled HSAs (via a Schwab Health Savings Brokerage Account and a guided HSA portfolio) with an employer dashboard for contributions and administration, positioning itself around transparent, zero-hidden-fee pricing. Backed by Costanoa Ventures and GGV Capital, Lively integrates with benefit administration platforms and third-party administrators but does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; integration is handled through its sales and partnerships channels. This profile was surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Lively's public web surface.

providers.name: Proximie
providers.description: Proximie is a health-tech company building a cloud platform it describes as the operating system for intelligent operating rooms, connecting surgical teams, medical devices, and data for remote telementoring, telesurgery, session recording, and AI-powered surgical insights across 500+ facilities in 50 countries. For developers, Proximie ships a pre-release C++ SDK (media streaming and session management, with an internal REST layer) and runs a Development Partners program that lets OEMs and medtech companies embed real-time connectivity, secure data routing, and white-label collaboration into their own devices. Proximie also open-sources WebRTC/Janus tooling (jarust, janus-mobile-sdk). Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund.

providers.name: QUIBIM
providers.description: QUIBIM is a healthcare AI company that unlocks medical imaging data to improve patient outcomes through quantitative imaging biomarkers and radiomics. Its cloud-based, tissue-agnostic platform ingests, harmonizes, and analyzes imaging data (MRI, CT, PET) to extract automated radiomics and deep-learning imaging biomarkers that support clinical decision-making and biopharma drug development. Regulated clinical products include QP-Prostate, QP-Brain, QP-Liver, QP-Breast, QP-Lung, and the QP-Insights multi-omics platform, several of which are CE and UKCA marked and integrate with hospital PACS systems. QUIBIM is ISO 27001:2022 certified and HIPAA and GDPR compliant. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; QUIBIM publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: AMBOSS
providers.description: AMBOSS is a Berlin-based (AMBOSS SE) digital medical knowledge platform used by medical students, physicians, educators, and healthcare institutions worldwide. It combines a physician-authored medical library, exam-style Qbanks with AI-powered analytics, and a point-of-care clinical reference tool, plus AI features (LiSA) for evidence-based clinical decision support. AMBOSS sells consumer memberships and institutional licenses to medical schools, residency programs, and hospitals. It is a Partech portfolio company. This profile was enriched from AMBOSS' public web and security surface; the medical platform publishes no public developer API (its amboss-mededu GitHub org hosts internal tooling), so this repo carries identity and security artifacts rather than API specifications.

providers.name: Apprentice
providers.description: Apprentice (apprentice.io) is an AI-native manufacturing platform for the life sciences, delivering Tempo Manufacturing Cloud — a GxP-compliant SaaS suite that unifies a Manufacturing Execution System (MES), Laboratory Execution System (LES), Augmented Work Instructions (AWI), and the Tandem collaboration/guest layer across pharmaceutical, biotech, and cell-and-gene-therapy sites. Tempo digitizes batch records, recipe authoring, and quality data from raw materials to finished goods, and exposes a RESTful Apprentice Public API (7.4+) for integrating Tempo data and metadata with external systems. The platform is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022 certified and validated to FDA 21 CFR Part 11. Backed by ICONIQ Capital. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from public surfaces; the Public API reference is gated to customers via their delivery lead / CSM.

providers.name: Blooming Health
providers.description: Blooming Health is an AI-powered, omnichannel care-management and community-engagement platform for healthcare and social-services organizations. It lets teams design multilingual care workflows across voice, SMS, and email in minutes — automating screening and needs assessments, service recommendations, outreach, appointment reminders, wellness check-ins, emergency broadcasts, closed-loop referral tracking, and Medicaid/SNAP recertification. The platform integrates with existing EHR/CRM systems and databases via FHIR, HL7, API, and SFTP, and is HIPAA compliant with encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access controls, audit trails, BAAs, and SOC 2 documentation available on request. Blooming Health is a healthcare portfolio company of Insight Partners. It exposes an enterprise integration surface but publishes no public developer portal or API reference.

providers.name: Impulse Dynamics
providers.description: Impulse Dynamics is a medical-device company that created Cardiac Contractility Modulation (CCM) therapy, delivered by the implantable Optimizer Smart and Optimizer Smart Mini pulse generators for patients with moderate-to-severe chronic heart failure who remain symptomatic despite guideline-directed medical therapy. Incorporated in 1997, with US headquarters in Marlton, New Jersey, the company won the first-ever FDA Breakthrough Device designation and received FDA approval for the Optimizer Smart in March 2019; the device has been CE marked since October 2016 and is now approved in more than 30 countries plus China. Impulse Dynamics operates no developer programme: there is no developer portal, API documentation, API reference, SDK, CLI, sandbox, pricing or sign-up, and nothing clinical or device-related is exposed as an API. It is catalogued here because its corporate website runs a live, anonymous, self-describing WordPress REST API advertising 420 routes across 30 namespaces, because that same install exposes two Model Context Protocol servers, and because the company publishes a substantive vulnerability disclosure programme with two PGP-published security contacts covering its medical devices, health software and infrastructure.

providers.name: Plume Health
providers.description: Plume Health (Plume) is a telehealth company delivering gender-affirming care to transgender and gender non-conforming people across the United States. Through a mobile app and licensed clinicians, Plume provides gender-affirming hormone therapy (estrogen and testosterone), mental health support, medical letters for surgery and identification changes, and everyday clinical care, all on a monthly membership subscription. Founded in 2019 and backed by General Catalyst, Plume operates as a HIPAA-covered, LegitScript-certified consumer healthcare provider. It is a consumer-facing care service and does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Radial Analytics
providers.description: Radial Analytics (Radial) is a Concord, Massachusetts healthcare technology company providing an AI/ML-powered clinical decision-support platform for the value-based care market. Its HIPAA-compliant, SOC 2 Type II certified software helps ACOs, hospitals, health systems, payers, and Medicare Advantage plans account for millions of clinical, claims, and quality datapoints to improve patient outcomes while reducing cost of care. Products include Radial Care, ACO Compare, Opportunity Navigator, decision-support modules, care pathways, and TEAM bundles. The company was founded by MIT PhDs Thaddeus Fulford-Jones and Eric Weiss and is backed by Initialized Capital. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company profile; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK.

providers.name: Tava Health
providers.description: Tava Health, Inc. is a Utah-founded (2019) digital behavioral-health company that sells mental health care as an employer and health-plan benefit. Employers, health plans and provider groups contract with Tava; covered members are matched to a licensed therapist — typically within about twelve hours — and receive care over secure video or in person through a nationwide clinical network. Care is delivered by Tava Professionals, a set of state-level professional entities that act as the HIPAA covered entity, while Tava Health, Inc. operates the technology platform as their business associate. The platform runs as two portals: a client portal at care.tavahealth.com for members and a provider/administrative portal at app.tavahealth.com for therapists and plan administrators. Tava also runs DirectCare, a partner-facing product with its own developer hub at docs.tavahealth.com; that hub is a ReadMe.io site and is password-protected, so no public API reference, OpenAPI definition or other machine-readable contract is available at this time.

providers.name: 9am Health
providers.description: 9amHealth (join9am.com) is a US virtual cardiometabolic clinic delivering specialized care for type 2 diabetes, obesity/weight loss, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol entirely from home. Founded in 2021 in San Diego by mySugr co-founders Frank Westermann and Anton Kittelberger, the company pairs at-home lab test kits, asynchronous and synchronous telehealth visits with obesity specialists, pharmacists, dietitians, and behavioral health experts, mail-order pharmacy for prescriptions including GLP-1 receptor agonists, and optional connected devices such as continuous glucose monitors into individualized care plans. It sells direct to individuals and through employers, health plans, and pharmacy benefit managers. 9amHealth is a consumer and enterprise telehealth brand and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation program; this profile captures its public web identity for the API Evangelist network. Backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: Workit Health
providers.description: Workit Health is a 100% virtual addiction-treatment provider delivering telehealth care for opioid use disorder, alcohol use disorder, and kratom/7-OH dependence via mobile app and video visits with licensed clinicians. Care includes FDA-approved medications such as Suboxone (buprenorphine/naloxone) and naltrexone, recovery groups, and asynchronous care-team messaging, serving members across fourteen US states. Backed by Insight Partners and Lux Capital. Workit Health publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: BostonGene
providers.description: BostonGene is a Waltham, Massachusetts precision-oncology company that combines an in-house CLIA-certified and CAP-accredited clinical laboratory with an AI-powered bioinformatics platform. It integrates whole-exome and whole-transcriptome sequencing, liquid biopsy (cfDNA/cfRNA), single-cell RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, spatial proteomics and digital pathology into multimodal molecular and immune profiling. Its clinical products include the Tumor Portrait test, immune system profiling, an immunohistochemistry (IHC) test and an Unknown Primary test; its biopharma services cover target analysis, biomarker discovery, clinical trial support, drug indication expansion and unmet-need identification. BostonGene publishes open-source research software (Kassandra cell deconvolution, Molecular Functional Portraits, pyigmap) on GitHub, but exposes no public developer API, SDK or API documentation; clinician ordering and report delivery run through an authenticated Salesforce Experience Cloud customer portal.

providers.name: Carecloud
providers.description: CareCloud (NASDAQ: CCLD, formerly MTBC) is a cloud-based healthcare technology company serving 45,000+ providers with an integrated platform spanning electronic health records (EHR), practice management, revenue cycle management (RCM), patient experience tools, and AI-driven clinical documentation (cirrusAI). Its Connector product delivers healthcare interoperability with FHIR and C-CDA data exchange across labs, EHRs, immunization registries, and diagnostics. CareCloud is Drummond-certified ONC Health IT and Surescripts-certified, publishes HIPAA compliance content, and operates a developer portal (AWS API Gateway) at developer.carecloud.com. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: DigitalOwl
providers.description: DigitalOwl is an AI-powered platform that transforms unstructured medical records into structured, actionable data for the life insurance, property & casualty insurance, and legal industries. Its products (View, Triage, Connect, Chat, Workflows, and Case Notes) automate medical record review, summarization, triage, and data extraction to accelerate underwriting, claims processing, and legal demand-package analysis. The Connect Data API maps source documents, classifications, and medical mentions (conditions, procedures, medications) into structured layers for integration into existing carrier and law-firm systems. DigitalOwl operates on AWS and Google Cloud with SOC 2 (Type II), HIPAA, and GDPR compliance. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Greater Good Health
providers.description: Greater Good Health is a Manhattan Beach, California value-based senior healthcare organization founded in 2021 that delivers preventive, whole-person primary care to older adults through a nurse-practitioner-led model. It operates its own senior primary care clinics and an integrated clinical services platform — risk adjustment and annual wellness visits, transitions of care, high-risk and chronic condition management, and behavioral health — delivered on behalf of health plans, medical groups, ACOs and other risk-bearing organizations. Alongside care delivery it runs a nurse practitioner community, the Greater Good Institute education portal, and clinical technology and analytics tooling for its employed NPs. It is a care delivery organization rather than a software vendor: it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Headway
providers.description: Headway operates a national mental-health care platform that connects patients, therapists and psychiatrists, and insurance companies. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in New York, Headway builds the first asset-free national network of behavioral-health providers who accept insurance, handling insurance credentialing, claims management, payments, and scheduling for clinicians while letting patients search for in-network providers, book appointments online, and see costs up front. The company partners with 45+ major insurers (Aetna, Anthem, Cigna, Oxford, UnitedHealthcare, Oscar) and, as of 2026, powers 600,000+ appointments per month across all 50 states. Headway is backed by a16z, Thrive, Accel, GV, Spark Capital, and Forerunner. It maintains SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance. Headway does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Judi Health
providers.description: Judi Health (formerly Capital Rx) is a healthcare technology company delivering unified pharmacy and medical benefit administration. Its platform, Judi, is a modern claims and benefits processing system (a Core Administrative Processing System / CAPS) that self-funded employers, unions, health plans, third-party administrators (TPAs), brokers, and health systems use to run transparent, pass-through pharmacy benefit management (Judi Rx), integrated health benefit administration (Judi Care), care navigation, level-funded pharmacy benefits, a Medicare prescription payment plan, and white-label discount cards. Judi Cloud licenses the underlying platform to other administrators. In 2026 the company rebranded from Capital Rx to Judi Health following a $400M funding round to accelerate its AI-powered health benefits platform, and its PBM business surpassed five million contracted lives. Judi Health does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API reference; this profile captures the company identity, web properties, and security/trust posture.

providers.name: Nolla Health
providers.description: Nolla Health is a Norway-born, AI-powered telehealth and dermatology company that entered the U.S. market with a $4.5M seed round led by General Catalyst and set up its headquarters in New York City. After treating more than 50,000 patients in Europe and becoming one of Norway's top-five medical apps, Nolla launched an AI-guided skin and acne care platform across 40+ U.S. states. The service pairs proprietary AI symptom assessment with clinician-in-the-loop oversight: patients complete a guided chat, a licensed U.S. medical provider reviews and approves every diagnosis and prescription, and topical medications are shipped directly to the patient. Nolla operates as a consumer-facing product (per-consultation and a monthly subscription) rather than an API provider, and publicly states HIPAA and GDPR compliance.

providers.name: Trusted Health
providers.description: Trusted Health is a career marketplace and workforce platform for travel nurses and allied health professionals across the United States. Clinicians build a single Trusted profile and get matched to travel and per-diem assignments, with transparent pay, licensure and compact-state guidance, and support through onboarding, credentialing, and placement. Its Works.AI product gives healthcare employers an AI-assisted staffing and workforce-management tool. Backed by Craft Ventures, Trusted Health operates a consumer web and mobile application (app.trustedhealth.com) rather than a public developer API; no OpenAPI, developer portal, or SDK surface is published. This profile captures the company's real security, trust, and compliance posture.

providers.name: Alzheon
providers.description: Alzheon, Inc. is a privately held clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2013 and headquartered at 111 Speen Street, Framingham, Massachusetts, developing oral small-molecule therapeutics and diagnostics for Alzheimer's disease and other neurodegenerative disorders. Its lead candidate, valiltramiprosate (ALZ-801) — a valine-conjugated prodrug of tramiprosate that blocks the formation of neurotoxic soluble beta-amyloid oligomers — has FDA Fast Track designation and completed the pivotal APOLLOE4 Phase 3 trial in APOE4/4 homozygotes with early Alzheimer's disease. Alzheon operates no product or developer API and publishes no developer portal, SDKs or API documentation; its corporate site does serve the standard WordPress REST API anonymously, which makes its press releases, science pages and media library machine-readable.

providers.name: Better Health
providers.description: Better Health (Better Health Supplies) is a modern, direct-to-consumer medical supplier that ships home medical supplies for chronic conditions straight to patients' doorsteps. The company covers diabetes and continuous glucose monitors (CGMs), incontinence, urology and self-catheterization, ostomy, and wound care categories, carrying leading brands and pairing product fulfillment with insurance-benefit navigation and one-on-one peer and clinical support. Better Health operates a Shopify-based storefront at joinbetter.com plus an education-focused community blog, and is backed by General Catalyst. It is cataloged in the API Evangelist network as a healthcare company profile; it publishes a consumer commerce experience rather than a first-party developer API, so this record captures its public web, security, and identity surface.

providers.name: Counsel Health
providers.description: Counsel Health is a telemedicine company multiplying the world's healthcare capacity by pairing an AI medical assistant with board-certified physicians delivered through chat. Individuals get free AI medical guidance and can connect with a licensed doctor for a flat $29 per consultation, seven days a week, for urgent care, primary care support, medication refills, lab testing, and health-record management. Counsel also ships an embedded product — a WebView / iFrame surface plus a server-side Counsel API — that partners integrate into their own applications, documented at docs.counselhealth.com with example apps published on GitHub. Backed by GV (Google Ventures).

providers.name: ianacare
providers.description: ianacare ("iana" = I Am Not Alone) is a Boston-based caregiver support and navigation platform that sells to employers, health plans and providers as a benefit for the working family caregivers in their populations. Founded in 2018 by Jessica Kim and Steven Lee, it pairs a consumer mobile app — where a caregiver mobilizes an informal care team, coordinates practical tasks, unlocks employer benefits and finds local resources — with human Caregiver Navigators, and positions itself as a partner for fulfilling CMS GUIDE Model dementia-care requirements. The company raised a $12.1M Series A in January 2022 led by Greycroft with 8VC, SemperVirens, Able Partners and the Brown Angel Group. ianacare ships software only as an end-user product: the iOS and Android apps and the app.ianacare.com web client are backed by first-party hosts (iana.ianacare.com behind a JWT bearer token, api.ianacare.com behind a CloudFront 403) and by ianacare's own Auth0 custom domain auth.ianacare.com, which is the single machine-readable contract the company publishes. There is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, SDK, CLI, webhook catalog, MCP server or agent card on any ianacare host.

providers.name: Stack Health
providers.description: Stack Healthcare (stackhealthcare.com) is a health-insurance fintech offering affordable, flexible coverage for small businesses and their teams. Operating as a technology company rather than a bank, Stack acts as a HIPAA Business Associate to employer-sponsored health plans, processing Protected Health Information for enrollment and benefits administration, and partners with Stripe for payments and Celtic Bank for issuing commercial cards. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Stack publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface — the product is a waitlist-gated web application — so this profile captures the identity, security, and compliance posture that is publicly verifiable.

providers.name: Angle Health
providers.description: Angle Health is a San Francisco-based, AI-native health insurance company offering full-stack, level-funded group health plans for small and mid-sized employers. Its platform pairs rapid, firm, bindable quoting with a modern benefits-administration experience that integrates with 100+ payroll and HRIS systems, a member care team, iOS/Android mobile apps, and pharmacy benefits (AngleRx). Angle also runs a partner API platform that lets quoting platforms, broker technology providers, and MGAs generate fully underwritten, firm, bindable level-funded quotes in minutes, along with automated proposal generation and member health scorecards with risk and cost-driver analysis. Developer documentation lives in an access-on-request partner portal.

providers.name: Beaconcure
providers.description: Beaconcure is a clinical data technology company whose AI-enabled platform, Verify, automates the statistical analysis and reporting workflow for biometrics teams running clinical trials. Verify converts static Tables, Listings and Figures (TLFs) into machine-readable form and runs format, reference, within-table and cross-table validation checks, tracks quality-control progress in a shared review workspace, and captures every fix in an inspection-ready audit trail across its Essentials, Validate and Generate modules. Beaconcure also documents a customer-scoped Verify REST API that exposes near real-time QC data — deliverables, projects, protocols, users, files, suspected and verified outputs, and discrepancies — as JSON or CSV, though each customer receives a unique API version and endpoint behind an IP allowlist. Founded in Israel with US headquarters in Boston, the company works with top-10 pharmaceutical companies and contract research organizations.

providers.name: Limbic
providers.description: Limbic is a clinical AI company for mental healthcare, founded in 2020 and headquartered in New York with a London engineering base. Its two products — Limbic Access, a Class IIa (UKCA) medical device for conversational patient intake, assessment and clinical decision support, and Limbic Care, an AI companion delivering guided CBT and on-demand support between therapy sessions — are embedded by health plans, health systems, behavioral health providers and NHS Talking Therapies services. Both are built on the proprietary "Limbic Layer", a clinical reasoning layer that sits between the user and a large language model to enforce validated clinical guidance. Limbic Access embeds into a provider website with a small script snippet rather than a public developer API; the company publishes no developer portal, OpenAPI definitions or SDKs, and integrates with EHR and patient management systems through customer engagements. Research code accompanying its peer-reviewed studies (including work published in Nature Medicine) is open on GitHub.

providers.name: TytoCare
providers.description: TytoCare is an AI-powered remote physical examination and virtual care company. Its FDA-cleared handheld examination device and Home Smart Clinic / Pro Smart Clinic platforms let clinicians remotely examine heart, lungs, ears, throat, skin, and temperature, serving 240+ healthcare organizations and 1.6M+ patients. TytoCare publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or client SDKs — EHR and telehealth integrations are delivered through private partner channels. An Insight Partners portfolio company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Waterlily
providers.description: Waterlily is an AI-native, end-to-end long-term care (LTC) planning platform for financial advisors, insurance professionals, and the families they serve. Trained on more than 500 million data points, its models predict an individual's personalized likelihood of needing long-term care, project the cost and duration of that care, and estimate the caregiving hours each family member is likely to contribute. A roughly three-minute intake produces a personalized care timeline and plan with localized cost estimates, and its Quote-and-Apply engine computes mathematically optimal LTC insurance policy configurations across hundreds of thousands of options. Founded by Lily Vittayarukskul and backed by Insight Partners. Waterlily is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company; it exposes no public developer API today (integrations are one-click CRM imports for Salesforce, Wealthbox, and Redtail).

providers.name: Champions Oncology
providers.description: Champions Oncology (NASDAQ: CSBR) is a global preclinical and clinical oncology contract research organization (CRO) supporting pharmaceutical and biotech drug development from discovery through the clinic. It maintains a living bank of more than 1,400 patient-derived tumor models and primary hematological models, and offers proprietary in vivo and ex vivo platforms, next-generation sequencing (WES/RNASeq), quantitative and phospho-proteomics, flow cytometry, and other analytical assays. Its Lumin Bioinformatics platform is an integrated, no-code analytics and visualization solution built on precisely curated multi-omics oncology data assembled from over 12,000 cancer patients, exposing gene networks, molecular signatures, target discovery, and AI-driven predictive analytics to researchers. Champions was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Stepful
providers.description: Stepful is a New York-based healthcare workforce education company that trains people with a high-school education for entry-level allied-health roles in as little as four months. It runs live, cohort-based online programs — Medical Assistant, Pharmacy Technician, Patient Care Technician, Medical Administrative Assistant, Surgical Technologist, Dental Assistant, Phlebotomy Technician, Sterile Processing and Practical Nursing — pairing virtual instructor-led classes and 1:1 coaching with at-home clinical skills kits, employer-site clinical rotations and an AI-assisted practice platform, then places graduates into hospital and clinic jobs. Its "School-as-a-Service" employer product lets health systems stand up in-house training and upskilling pipelines. Stepful is backed by Y Combinator, Oak HC/FT and Reach Capital, has raised a $31.5M Series B and a $55M Series C, and reports having served more than 30,000 students. It is a Delaware corporation approved to operate by state career-school boards in Alabama, California, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Texas and Utah. Stepful publishes no public developer API: its student classroom and staff admin applications are both authenticated-only, and no OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP or webhook contract is served from any host it controls.

providers.name: Dutch
providers.description: Dutch (dutch.com) is a United States pet telemedicine service that gives dog and cat owners 24/7 access to licensed online veterinarians through a low-cost membership (from about $11/month), pairing virtual vet visits with free prescription delivery to most states. Founded to bring the direct-to-consumer telehealth model to pet care, Dutch is backed by Forerunner Ventures. The public presence is a consumer telehealth storefront hosted on Shopify; at the time of profiling no first-party public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface was found. This API Evangelist profile captures the company's real, published web surface (identity, policies, account, support) and the live platform-level discovery documents exposed on the domain.

providers.name: Findoctave
providers.description: Findoctave (operating as Octave) is a mental health care provider offering virtual and in-person therapy across 20+ U.S. states. Services include individual, couples, and family therapy, DBT, and specialized centers of excellence for perinatal and postpartum health, LGBTQIA+ (queer resiliency), trauma, and women's emotional health. Octave is in-network with major insurers (Aetna, Blue Shield of California, BCBS plans, Health Net, and others) and publishes a therapist directory, cost calculator, and getting-started flow through its consumer website. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Felicis and added to the API Evangelist network; Octave exposes no public developer API, so this profile is a company identity record rather than an API listing.

providers.name: NeuroFlow
providers.description: NeuroFlow is a Philadelphia-based behavioral health technology company that gives payers, health systems, provider groups and federal agencies the infrastructure to identify and manage behavioral health risk at scale. Its IntegrateBH platform pairs patient-facing mobile and web applications with measurement-based care and screening workflows, clinical dashboards, care-coordination tooling and population-level behavioral health analytics. The platform reaches customers through EHR and partner integrations — including Epic (App Orchard / Epic Showroom) and the Xealth digital-health ecosystem — over a session-authenticated REST API served from neuroflowlive.com/api/. NeuroFlow publishes no public developer portal: a Swagger document exists at /api/swagger.json on every environment, but it returns HTTP 401 "Please log in to continue" to anonymous callers, so the contract is customer-only.

providers.name: Triple-S Management
providers.description: Triple-S Management Corporation is the largest managed care company in Puerto Rico in terms of membership, providing health, life, and property and casualty insurance. A subsidiary of GuideWell (parent of Florida Blue), Triple-S operates as an independent licensee of the Blue Cross Blue Shield Association for Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Its subsidiaries include Triple-S Salud (managed care), Triple-S Advantage (Medicare Advantage), Triple-S Vida (life insurance), Triple-S Propiedad (property and casualty), Salus (medical clinics), and CarePoint (IPA).

providers.name: Fortuna Health
providers.description: Fortuna Health is a consumer-first Medicaid navigation platform that helps patients and members move through the Medicaid enrollment, recertification, appeals, and coverage-management processes end to end. Founded in 2023 and based in New York City, Fortuna consolidates the fragmented rules of the 50+ state and territory Medicaid programs — each with its own eligibility rules, documentation standards, and renewal timelines — into a single digital interface. The platform lets consumers connect accounts that auto-populate their filings, provides a virtual mailbox for state and health-plan communications, and sends text notifications for urgent, time-sensitive actions. Fortuna partners with health systems and managed care plans as middleware for the roughly $800B Medicaid ecosystem, and is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Y Combinator.

providers.name: House Rx
providers.description: House Rx is a healthcare technology company that equips independent specialty and community clinics to run in-house, medically integrated dispensing pharmacies. Founded in 2021, its cloud platform — built by specialty pharmacists and physicians — supports the full specialty-medication workflow: prior authorization, financial counseling and copay assistance, fulfillment tools, scalable patient outreach and messaging, real-time operational analytics, and EHR integration so physicians and pharmacists collaborate on patient care. House Rx is SOC 2 compliant and backed by First Round, Bessemer Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, Maverick Ventures, 1984 Ventures, and Character Ventures. House Rx does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its company identity, security posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: Parachute Health
providers.description: Parachute Health is the leading digital platform for durable medical equipment (DME), home medical equipment, and medical supply ePrescribing. Clinicians eSign and submit DME orders in seconds, and the platform coordinates in real time across a network of 3,000+ supplier locations, 270,000+ eSigning clinicians, and 70,000+ facilities in all 50 states. Parachute integrates with EHR/EMR systems (athenahealth, PointClickCare, Epic, and others) using HL7 2.x and FHIR interfaces, and offers prior-authorization automation, health-plan workflows, and value-based-care coordination. Integration is delivered as private, partner-provisioned EMR/HL7/FHIR interfaces rather than a public self-service developer API.

providers.name: Attuned Intelligence
providers.description: Attuned Intelligence is a healthcare voice AI company that automates hospital and community health center call centers with supervised, EHR-integrated Voice AI Agents. Its agents answer every patient call instantly and in the caller's language, resolve needs end-to-end (appointment booking, medication refills, triage routing), and provide real-time human oversight with transcripts and reporting so automation stays safe and auditable. Founded in 2024 by leaders from DeepMind, Google Health, AssemblyAI, and DocuSign, the company emerged from stealth in October 2025 with $13M in funding backed by Threshold Ventures, and serves customers including Cambridge Health Alliance and Lowell Community Health Center. The platform is SOC 2 and HIPAA compliant. Attuned publishes no first-party developer/product API; its Wix-hosted marketing site exposes a generic hosted Site MCP endpoint for agentic access to public site content and business details.

providers.name: BestDoc
providers.description: BestDoc is a healthcare patient-relationship-management (PRM) company that helps hospitals improve the patient experience across inpatient and outpatient care. Its platform includes BestDoc Concierge for inpatient experience management (non-clinical requests, room food ordering, discharge management), BestDoc Practice for outpatient patient-request management, BestDoc Survey for omni-channel patient feedback, an AI Reply Assistant for automated review responses, and continued-care engagement tools. BestDoc integrates with hospital information systems (HIS), EMRs, and payment gateways. BestDoc Technology Pvt. Ltd. is an ISO 27001:2013 certified company operating from Kochi, Bangalore, and Dubai. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Caidya
providers.description: Caidya is a full-service, global clinical research organization (CRO) formed from the April 2021 merger of dMed and Clinipace, rebranded to Caidya in October 2022. It runs clinical development programs end to end — pre-IND and regulatory strategy, early phase, Phase II/III delivery, study start-up, trial feasibility, clinical operations, risk-based quality management, medical monitoring, clinical data management, biometrics, medical writing, pharmacovigilance, quality assurance and post-marketing surveillance — across oncology and hematology, cardiovascular-metabolic, rare disease, pediatrics, gastroenterology, nephrology, dermatology, ophthalmology, cell and gene therapy, neurology, immunology and infectious disease. The company took a $165M strategic growth investment from Rubicon Founders and announced a strategic combination with Simbec-Orion. Caidya is a clinical services provider rather than a software vendor: it integrates with sponsor-preferred EDC, eCOA, IRT, CTMS, eTMF and safety platforms rather than publishing a developer program or a public API of its own.

providers.name: CareRev
providers.description: CareRev is a healthcare workforce management and on-demand labor marketplace that connects hospitals and health systems directly with local, credentialed clinical professionals — registered nurses, LPN/LVNs, CNAs, surgical and ER techs, medical assistants, respiratory therapists, phlebotomists and mental health techs — without a traditional staffing agency in the middle. Facilities post open shifts from their existing scheduling and HR systems and vetted clinicians browse, claim and self-schedule them in the CareRev mobile app, while CareRev handles credential verification, compliance and payment. The product line spans the CareRev Marketplace (external on-demand talent), IRP+ (internal resource pool control and float-pool visibility for a health system's own staff) and Smart Rates (dynamic rate modeling to control labor spend). CareRev is certified by The Joint Commission under its Health Care Staffing Services program and serves more than 650 facilities across the United States. Integration with a facility's VMS, scheduling and workforce-management stack (including UKG Dimensions via the UKG Connect Technology Partner Program) is delivered through private, partner-scoped API connections; CareRev publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable API contract as of this profiling pass.

providers.name: Chefaa
providers.description: Chefaa is Egypt's leading digital pharmacy and pharmacy-benefits platform, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Cairo. Its GPS-enabled, AI-powered consumer app connects more than 1.5 million monthly users with a nationwide network of over 1,500 partner pharmacies, letting patients upload, order, schedule, and refill both insured and non-insured prescriptions with home delivery, medication reminders, and pharmacist chat support. On the B2B side Chefaa operates a full-stack supply layer for pharmacies and corporates — including Chefaa Supply (direct procurement with deferred payment and consolidated delivery) and the Makhazen pharmacy-supply app — plus the Chefaa Prime subscription for SMEs and consumers. Chefaa is a 500 Global portfolio company. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; Chefaa publishes consumer and B2B web/mobile products but does not expose a public developer API program, so the enrichment below is limited to its public web, security, and domain surface.

providers.name: Dedalus
providers.description: Dedalus Group is a European healthcare and diagnostics software provider headquartered in Florence, Italy, supplying clinical information systems, electronic patient records, laboratory and diagnostic imaging software to hospitals, laboratories and care networks across roughly 40 countries. Its product estate includes the ORBIS and ORBIS U electronic patient record suites, the Lorenzo EPR in the UK, X1.V1 in Italy, and DC4H (Digital Connect 4 Health) / Open Health Connect, an HL7 FHIR-based interoperability and longitudinal-patient-record platform the company markets under an "API economy" model. Dedalus states that DC4H exposes an FHIR API management component that third-party developers can build against, and the company participates in the openEHR community, but as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI or FHIR CapabilityStatement, and no sandbox on any dedalus.com host — integration access runs through a sales and customer-support motion rather than a self-serve developer surface.

providers.name: EDDA Technology
providers.description: EDDA Technology, Inc. is a Princeton, New Jersey medical imaging software company behind the IQQA platform for computer-assisted radiology and surgery. IQQA delivers 3D quantitative image analysis, automated segmentation and volumetric measurement over CT and MR studies, supporting pre-surgical planning and simulation, intra-operative guidance and monitoring, post-operative follow-up evaluation, and clinical training across liver, lung, kidney and interventional oncology. Products include IQQA-BodyImaging, IQQA-Guide, IQQA-Chest, IQQA-Liver, IQQA-Liver Function, IQQA-eQMR and the IQQA-eFusion edge-AI surgical navigation system. The company is FDA cleared and CE marked under EU MDR 2017/745, and raised a US$150 million round led by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 with OrbiMed participation in April 2021. EDDA publishes no developer API for IQQA — it is regulated medical device software deployed on-premises in hospitals — so the only public API surface catalogued here is the WordPress REST API serving eddatech.com content.

providers.name: Eden Health
providers.description: Eden Health was a primary and virtual care company that delivered app-based medical care, behavioral health, and care navigation to employers and their employees, integrating with health systems and insurers (backed by Insight Partners). It was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Its public marketing site is no longer reachable over TLS, but its primary backend service — the "Grdn" (Guardian) API at api.edenhealth.com — still serves a Swagger 2.0 description covering patients, appointments, membership, documents, care teams, and clinician tooling.

providers.name: Genalyte
providers.description: Genalyte, Inc. is a San Diego, California in-vitro diagnostics company building point-of-care blood testing systems based on silicon photonic microring resonator technology. Founded by Cary Gunn, the company developed the Maverick Diagnostic System and its successor Merlin, an automated benchtop analyzer that runs hematology, chemistry and immunoassay panels — including CBC, lipid panel and comprehensive metabolic panel — from small whole-blood or serum volumes and returns results in roughly twenty to thirty minutes while the patient is still in the clinic. A cloud verification layer the company markets as CloudLab quality-checks results and routes them into electronic medical record systems. Genalyte received FDA clearance for a thyroid stimulating hormone immunoassay performed on a silicon chip and previously held an FDA Emergency Use Authorization for a rapid COVID-19 antibody test. The company is investor-backed (Khosla Ventures, Verily Life Sciences and others) and is a HIPAA covered entity that publishes a Notice of Privacy Practices. As of this profile Genalyte publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Insightec
providers.description: Insightec Ltd. is an Israeli medical device company, founded in 1999 and headquartered in Tirat Carmel, Israel, that develops and sells MR-guided focused ultrasound (MRgFUS) systems under the Exablate brand. Its Exablate Neuro platform focuses more than a thousand ultrasound beams through the intact skull to ablate a target deep in the brain without an incision, and is approved for essential tremor and Parkinson's disease, including staged bilateral treatment. The Exablate body platform is used for uterine fibroids, palliation of bone metastases, and prostate indications, and the company runs clinical programs in blood-brain-barrier opening and glioblastoma. Insightec publishes a public product documentation portal of operator manuals and handbooks for the Exablate systems, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API contract, SDKs, or agent surface; its systems integrate with GE and Siemens MR scanners as clinical devices rather than through a public API.

providers.name: RefleXion Medical
providers.description: RefleXion Medical is a privately held therapeutic oncology company headquartered in Hayward, California, founded in 2009 by Sam Mazin and Akshay Nanduri around the biology-guided radiotherapy (BgRT) concept conceived at Stanford University in 2007. The company designs, manufactures and commercializes the RefleXion X1 radiotherapy platform and SCINTIX biology-guided radiotherapy, which uses onboard PET detectors to sense emissions from an injected radiopharmaceutical and autonomously direct external-beam radiotherapy delivery with sub-second latency. The RefleXion X1 received FDA clearance for SRS, SBRT and IMRT in 2020, and SCINTIX therapy was FDA cleared in February 2023 for treating tumors in the lung or bone arising from primary and metastatic cancer. RefleXion has raised more than $500 million from investors including TPG's The Rise Fund, KCK Group, PSP Investments, Sofinnova, Pfizer Ventures and Johnson & Johnson Innovation. RefleXion is a medical device manufacturer rather than a software vendor and publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Valera Health
providers.description: Valera Health is a Brooklyn, New York based virtual behavioral health provider delivering therapy, psychiatry, group therapy, comprehensive Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), suicide care and youth support programs to adults and children through an in-house clinical team, a care-coordinator model and a patient mobile app. It is a care-delivery organization rather than a software vendor: revenue comes from commercial insurance, Medicaid and Medicare reimbursement, and the clinical record and patient portal run on third-party health IT (the patient portal is operated by NextGen Healthcare at pxpportal.nextgen.com). As of this profile Valera Health publishes no developer program, no public API reference, and no machine-readable contract of any kind; its only externally addressable API host, api.valerahealth.com, is the private backend for its own patient application.

providers.name: Vektor Medical
providers.description: Vektor Medical is a San Diego based medical technology company whose vMap system is an FDA-cleared and CE-marked, AI-based arrhythmia mapping solution. vMap analyzes standard 12-lead ECG data and produces beat-by-beat 2D and 3D cardiac source maps across all four chambers of the heart in about a minute, without requiring an invasive catheter-based mapping procedure. Electrophysiologists use it for triage, procedural planning and ablation guidance across focal and fibrillation-type arrhythmias and atrial and ventricular pacing. The product is delivered as Software as a Medical Device to hospitals and health systems under clinical agreements. Vektor Medical publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: VuMedi
providers.description: VuMedi (Vumedi, Inc.) operates a video education platform for physicians and other healthcare professionals. Founded in 2008 and headquartered in Oakland, California, with offices in Saint Louis Park, Minnesota and Zagreb, Croatia, the platform aggregates a library of long-form educational videos, webinars, conference coverage and case discussions contributed by key opinion leaders and academic medical centers across more than twenty-five clinical specialties. Physicians use it to watch surgical technique videos, follow live and on-demand webinars, discuss cases with peers and presenters, and stay current on clinical evidence. The company monetizes through industry partnerships with pharmaceutical and medical-device brands rather than a subscription paywall. As of August 2026 VuMedi publishes no public developer program, API documentation, machine-readable API contract, SDKs or MCP server; its public surface is the consumer web application, an iOS app, and a set of static marketing and policy pages.

providers.name: Imagen
providers.description: Imagen (Imagen Technologies) is an AI-enabled, sub-specialized diagnostic imaging partner for independent practices, hospitals, and health systems. It combines in-clinic imaging equipment, FDA-cleared AI algorithms, and a 24/7 teleradiology network of fellowship-trained, board-certified specialists to deliver rapid, accurate radiology interpretations, plus advanced analytics for care-gap identification. Imagen operates across 23 states, serving roughly 3.5 million patients, and is backed by GV and Threshold Ventures. The company publishes a security program covering SOC 2 Type II, the HITRUST CSF, and HIPAA. Imagen Technologies exposes no public developer API surface at this time. (Note the distinct namesake company Imagen AI, imagen-ai.com, an AI photo-editing product that does publish an API and SDK.)

providers.name: Mirza
providers.description: Mirza is a public benefits infrastructure platform that helps government agencies, health plans and MCOs, health systems, and employers enroll people in social safety-net programs (Medicaid, SNAP, WIC, childcare subsidies, and more) and keep them covered as eligibility rules change. It matches individuals to 200+ benefits across all 50 states, verifies eligibility from existing data rather than paperwork, prevents disenrollment through early exemption detection, and generates audit-ready compliance documentation including H.R.1 Medicaid community-engagement support. Mirza integrates with existing eligibility systems rather than replacing them. Founded in 2020 by Siran Cao and Mel Faxon; backed by 500 Global and others.

providers.name: AccessHope
providers.description: AccessHope is a Los Angeles-area health benefits company, founded in 2019 and wholly owned by City of Hope, that delivers remote cancer expertise as an employer-sponsored benefit. Its subspecialist teams review a member's pathology, imaging, molecular testing and treatment plan against the latest evidence from a coalition of National Cancer Institute-designated Comprehensive Cancer Centers — City of Hope, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Emory Winship, Fred Hutch, Johns Hopkins Kimmel, Northwestern Medicine Lurie, and UT Southwestern Simmons — and return guidance to the member's own local oncologist rather than moving the patient. AccessHope reports roughly 9 million covered members across 700+ employer and health-plan clients, including 70+ Fortune 500 companies. Delivery is business-to-business: employers, benefits consultants, health plans and navigation partners onboard through an eligibility file feed and an implementation-managed workflow, while members and clinical staff use credentialed web portals. AccessHope publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Archy
providers.description: Archy is an all-in-one, cloud-based dental practice management platform that consolidates scheduling, clinical charting, imaging, insurance verification, billing, patient communication, online payments, and reporting into a single system, layered with AI agents (Scribe for clinical notes, Revenue for insurance claim posting, Intelligence for analytics, and Verify for real-time insurance verification) that automate routine practice workflows. Founded in 2021 by Jonathan Rat and Benjamin Kolin and backed by TCV, Bessemer Venture Partners, CRV, and Entree Capital, Archy has raised roughly $47M through a 2025 Series B and serves tens of thousands of active users across dental practices. As a handler of protected health information it is HIPAA-compliant, publishes a Vanta-hosted trust center, and ships native iOS and Android apps. Archy exposes no public developer API; this profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network for identity, security, and discoverability coverage.

providers.name: Carrot
providers.description: Carrot is a global fertility and family-building benefits platform that helps employers, health plans, benefits consultants, and labor unions offer inclusive reproductive care to their members. Carrot supports the full journey — preconception, IVF and IUI, egg, sperm, and embryo preservation, gestational surrogacy, adoption, pregnancy and postpartum care, men's health, and hormonal and menopause support — across 175+ countries and 17,000+ providers. Products include Carrot Intelligence (an AI clinical platform), Carrot Rx medication sourcing, the Carrot Card payment solution, and Carrot Sprints metabolic-fertility programs. Backed by CRV; added to the API Evangelist network from VC portfolio enrichment.

providers.name: Equip Health
providers.description: Equip Health is a virtual, evidence-based eating disorder treatment provider founded in 2019 by Kristina Saffran and Erin Parks. Equip delivers 100% remote, insurance-covered care for all eating disorder diagnoses — anorexia, bulimia, binge eating disorder (BED), ARFID, atypical anorexia, and OSFED — using Family-Based Treatment (FBT) and other evidence-based approaches. Every patient is matched with a five-person care team: a therapist, medical provider, dietitian, family mentor, and peer mentor. Equip serves patients across the United States with no waitlist, publishes an extensive library of clinical and recovery articles, partners with providers and health plans, and operates a patient portal at my.equip.health. This profile catalogs Equip's public web, legal, security, and content surfaces; Equip publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation program at this time.

providers.name: Hello Patient
providers.description: Hello Patient builds AI agents (branded "Mia") for patient conversations across voice, text, and web chat, helping healthcare practices automate their front office, back office, and patient-growth workflows. Mia handles 24/7 appointment scheduling, insurance verification, and patient intake on the front office; revenue-cycle (RCM) follow-up and no-show recovery on the back office; and lead conversion, patient recall, and targeted outreach for growth. The platform serves dentistry, dermatology, ENT, mental health, optometry, primary care, urgent care, veterinary, and consumer-health practices, and integrates with EHR and practice systems including ModMed, AdvancedMD, NextGen, eClinicalWorks, Athena Health, Veradigm, Zenoti, and others. Hello Patient is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type 2 certified. It is backed by 8VC and Scale Venture Partners. No public developer API is documented at this time; this profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: MedHOK (Hearst Communications)
providers.description: MHK (formerly MedHOK), part of Hearst Health, is a healthcare technology company providing a unified SaaS platform for health plans and payers. Its CareProminence suite spans utilization management, care management, complaints/appeals and grievances, pharmacy management, population health and quality management, and interoperability (the MHK Interop Suite), while its MarketProminence suite covers enrollment and member maintenance, premium billing, financial reconciliation, and member web portals. MHK helps Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial health plans streamline operations, ensure regulatory compliance, and improve the member experience. The MHK Interop Suite supports FHIR, SMART on FHIR, Da Vinci, and CMS-0057 interoperability requirements. MHK publishes HITRUST and ISO 27001 certification and NCQA prevalidation. The company operates a public marketing and resource site but does not publish a public developer portal or API program.

providers.name: Tendo
providers.description: Tendo is a healthcare software company founded in 2020 by siblings Dan and Jen Goldsmith (previously of Veeva Systems and Instructure) and headquartered in the Philadelphia area. Tendo builds a cloud, purpose-built healthcare platform and a suite of applications that connect patients, clinicians, providers, and caregivers across the care journey — spanning digital patient engagement, quality and clinical documentation improvement, hospital quality rankings analytics, and the Care Connect marketplace for employers, providers, and patients.
