providers.description: SteadyMD is a telehealth infrastructure and clinical-workforce company (a DocGo company) backed by Lux Capital. It supplies board-certified physicians and nurse practitioners, clinical operations, and 50-state licensing and credentialing, plus technology and telehealth APIs that let healthcare and digital-health partners launch branded, fully managed virtual care. Its APIs cover patient data submission, synchronous and asynchronous consult requests, two-way patient-clinician messaging, intake forms, clinician availability, real-time status updates, document attachments, scheduling, and reporting/SLA retrieval, offered as either a Limited (partner-EMR) or Complete (SteadyMD-EMR) integration. API documentation is provided under a business agreement via a request form; there is no public developer portal or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Tend
providers.description: Tend (Tend Dental) is a consumer dental-care company offering modern, judgment-free dentistry through a network of design-forward "studios" across New York City, Boston, Atlanta, Washington DC, Nashville and Connecticut. The brand pairs a soothing in-person studio experience and top-rated dentists with a fully online booking and patient-intake flow at hellotend.com. Services span preventive hygiene, family dental care, cosmetic dentistry, veneers, Invisalign and clear aligners, orthodontics, dental implants, endodontics, sedation and emergency care. Backed by GV and Redpoint Ventures. This is a consumer web/ booking business with no public developer API surface; the profile is enriched with identity, security-posture and discovery-probe artifacts only.

providers.name: Tennr
providers.description: Tennr is a New York City-based healthcare technology company (founded 2021) building agentic patient-orchestration software that automates referral-based care operations for providers and health systems. Its proprietary vision-language model, RaeLM, is trained on over 100 million anonymized medical documents to read faxes, referrals, and unstructured records, then automates document classification, data extraction, patient qualification, insurance eligibility verification, and prior-authorization submission by integrating directly with existing EHR systems. Tennr processes over 10 million documents monthly and is HIPAA and SOC 2 compliant. It raised a $101M Series C at a $605M valuation led by IVP, with a16z, Lightspeed, GV, ICONIQ, and Foundation Capital participating. Tennr does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or specification; integrations are delivered through EHR connections and professional services.

providers.name: Asepha
providers.description: Asepha is an AI workflow automation platform built specifically for pharmacies, positioning itself as "the context graph for the therapy-start journey" with a stated vision to make medication delays impossible. Its AI agents automate repetitive pharmacy operations across automated prescription data entry, back-office work, 340B management (TPA matching, accruals, purchase-order automation), medication reconciliation (Best Possible Medication History), a conversational voice call assistant, benefits verification and prior-authorization (BV/PA) automation, REMS compliance reporting, and medication therapy review. The company reports outcomes such as a 32% reduction in manual labour cost within one month and tasks completed 4x faster than baseline. Asepha is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and HIPAA compliant, with AES-256 encryption at rest. Founded by CEO Eunice Wu, PharmD and CTO Can Uncu, the company operates from New York, NY and Toronto, ON, and is a Techstars portfolio company. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Asepha publishes no public API, developer portal, or specifications at this time.

providers.name: Carta Healthcare
providers.description: Carta Healthcare, Inc. is a San Francisco based clinical data management company that applies a "Hybrid Intelligence" model — proprietary AI paired with certified human clinical abstractors — to extract, validate and submit structured clinical data on behalf of hospitals and health systems. Its product family covers Voyager (the underlying AI data platform trained on electronic medical record content), Lighthouse and Atlas (AI-assisted clinical registry abstraction and submission, including the ACC NCDR, STS/ACC TVT and Vascular Quality Initiative registries), Navigator (clinical data intelligence and analytics), Harbor (cohort selection and clinical trial matching) and outsourced expert abstraction services. Carta Healthcare is an NCDR certified software vendor and has completed a Type 2 SOC 2 examination with an unqualified opinion covering security, availability and confidentiality. The company sells and integrates directly with hospital EMR environments under enterprise agreements; it publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract on its public web surface.

providers.name: Doctronic
providers.description: Doctronic is a consumer telemedicine platform that pairs an AI doctor with licensed physicians for anonymous, low-cost health care. Users describe their symptoms to an AI assistant that performs a free symptom assessment and health consultation, then can escalate to a real doctor for a video visit ($39/visit), prescription refills, lab orders, and follow-up care. Positioned as "Free. Anonymous. Built by doctors," the product is direct-to-consumer web and mobile rather than a developer platform: it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation. The only public machine-readable surface is an RFC 9116 security.txt with a coordinated vulnerability-disclosure policy. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Hippocratic AI
providers.description: Hippocratic AI builds safety-focused generative AI agents for non-diagnostic healthcare tasks, powered by its Polaris constellation architecture. Polaris 5.0 is a multi-trillion-parameter constellation of specialized models clinically validated by U.S.-licensed clinicians. Hippocratic AI sells agents such as Nurse Co-Pilot and AI Front Door to health systems, payors, and life-sciences organizations through enterprise sales rather than a self-service public API.

providers.name: Joyful
providers.description: Joyful Health provides AI-assisted revenue recovery for healthcare organizations, combining automated claim investigation with expert billing teams to recover unpaid and denied insurance claims. Its platform runs inside an organization's existing revenue-cycle-management (RCM) systems rather than replacing them, covering denial investigation and root-cause analysis, claims recovery and appeals management, historical accounts-receivable (A/R) assessment, payer follow-up, documentation review, and financial insight to prevent future denials. The company operates a customer application at app.joyfulhealth.io and maintains a Vanta-hosted trust center. Joyful is a portfolio company of CRV. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; Joyful does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Lucem Health
providers.description: Lucem Health is a clinical-AI company founded in 2021 with Mayo Clinic Platform, backed by Mayo Clinic, Commure and Rally Ventures. Its Lucem Health Reveal programs apply clinically validated AI models to a health system's existing data to surface patients at elevated risk of serious or chronic disease — arrhythmias, colorectal cancer, liver disease, lung cancer and Type 1 diabetes — and deliver those insights into existing clinical workflows without changing how clinicians practice. The company also runs a Clinical AI SolutionOps practice that helps AI innovators and life-sciences organizations deploy, scale and commercialize models against provider data. Integration is delivered as a managed service into EHR, PACS and other clinical systems; as of 2026-08-25 Lucem Health publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: myLaurel
providers.description: myLaurel is a New York-based healthcare company delivering acute and transitional care in patients' homes. Its hybrid model pairs hands-on clinical teams with virtual technology support to prevent unnecessary hospitalizations, free critical hospital bed space, improve patient outcomes, and lower the total cost of care for both health systems and health plans. Reported results include a 49% reduction in 30-day readmissions, an average 1.5-day length-of-stay reduction, a 97 Net Promoter Score, and 3:1+ ROI within 90 days. myLaurel is a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures). This profile has been enriched from the company's public web surface; it currently exposes no public developer API.

providers.name: Pharmeasy
providers.description: PharmEasy is one of India's largest digital healthcare platforms, operating a consumer online pharmacy and health marketplace at pharmeasy.in. It lets users order prescription and over-the-counter medicines (with prescription upload and verification), buy health and wellness products, book diagnostic lab tests and health checkup packages, and consult doctors via telemedicine, plus a PLUS subscription for recurring savings. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Prosus Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. PharmEasy runs an internal API at api.pharmeasy.in but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI; it does operate a responsible-disclosure security program (infosec@pharmeasy.in). Sector: healthcare / e-pharmacy.

providers.name: PocketHealth
providers.description: PocketHealth is a patient-centric medical imaging platform that lets patients access, view, store, and share their diagnostic imaging (DICOM) and reports online, and lets healthcare providers exchange imaging across institutions and networks. PocketHealth also publishes an open, RESTful developer API aimed at RIS/PACS/VNA vendors, letting them embed PocketHealth's patient enrollment, electronic consent, and background record-delivery workflows natively into their own clinical software. The developer API is partner-gated - it is free forever for RIS/PACS vendors, healthcare providers, and physicians, but the full technical reference (base URL, endpoint paths, authentication) is not published on the open web; engaged vendors are assigned a dedicated integration rep who provides testing resources and detailed documentation. As a result the APIs below are modeled from PocketHealth's public developer-program descriptions rather than a public API reference or OpenAPI definition.

providers.name: Qventus
providers.description: Qventus is a healthcare technology company that provides an AI-powered automation platform for hospital operations. Its "AI teammates" combine machine learning, generative AI, and behavioral science to streamline care-coordination workflows across surgical growth and operating-room utilization, perioperative and pre-admission-testing coordination, inpatient capacity and discharge planning, and care-gap and coding automation. Qventus sells to health systems and hospitals as a B2B SaaS product and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners, Mayfield, Norwest Venture Partners, and Y Combinator.

providers.name: Solventum
providers.description: Solventum is a Fortune 500 healthcare company spun off from 3M in 2024, focused on healthcare technology including medical-surgical solutions, dental and orthodontic products, health information systems, and purification and filtration technologies. Solventum serves hospitals, clinics, dental practices, and healthcare IT organizations worldwide.

providers.name: Truemeds
providers.description: Truemeds is an India-based online pharmacy and digital healthcare platform operated by Intellihealth Solutions that lets consumers order branded and generic prescription and over-the-counter medicines for home delivery across India, typically positioned around savings on genuine medicines, free teleconsultation with doctors, and substitute-medicine recommendations. It runs a consumer web and mobile app experience (order medicines, upload prescriptions, health blog, help center) rather than a public developer API program; no public API documentation, developer portal, OpenAPI, or partner API surface was found during enrichment. Backed by Accel and other investors, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Bristle
providers.description: Bristle (Bristle Health) is a consumer health company that makes the world's first at-home oral microbiome saliva test, helping people measure, understand, and improve their oral health. Customers order a mail-in saliva collection kit, and Bristle sequences the oral microbiome to report on bacteria associated with cavities, gum disease, and bad breath, then pairs the results with guidance and a line of targeted oral-care products including probiotics. Bristle also works with dental professionals who offer microbiome testing to their patients. The company sells direct to consumers through a Shopify-hosted storefront at bristlehealth.com and is backed by Initialized Capital. There is no first-party public developer API; this profile captures Bristle's public web, commercial, and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Curve Dental
providers.description: Curve Dental is a cloud-based, all-in-one dental practice management software company founded in 2004 and headquartered in Alpharetta, Georgia. Its flagship platform, Curve Hero, serves more than 80,000 dental professionals across the United States and Canada, unifying scheduling, clinical and perio charting, imaging, billing, insurance, smart forms, reporting, patient engagement, and business analytics in a single browser-based system. Curve is privately held and backed by Battery Ventures, and connects to a growing ecosystem of integration partners (including DentalXChange, DentalHQ, Pearl AI, Bola AI, and Mango Voice) rather than exposing a public self-serve developer API. This profile was seeded from Battery Ventures' portfolio and enriched from Curve Dental's public web surface; no public OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Fertifa
providers.description: Fertifa is Europe's reproductive healthcare benefits provider for employers, giving companies a way to offer fertility, family-forming, women's health, maternity, menopause, men's reproductive health, and neurodiversity support to their employees. The platform pairs an in-house clinical team with education and training, diagnostics and testing, prescriptions and medication delivery, and financing/reimbursement, delivered to staff through a mobile app and to HR teams through enterprise and SME plans. Fertifa is London-based, backed by Speedinvest, and works with employers including Lululemon, Meta, Bain Capital, and Virgin. No public developer API or OpenAPI surface is currently published; this profile captures the company's public web, legal, and support properties.

providers.name: Flatiron Health
providers.description: Flatiron Health is a healthcare technology company focused on oncology, combining real-world data from millions of cancer patients with software and AI to support life sciences research and clinical care. Its platforms include OncoEMR and OncoCloud for oncology practices, Flatiron Vessel (clinical research EDC, formerly Protocol First) and Clinical Pipe for clinical trials, and real-world evidence products for life sciences. Flatiron data has informed thousands of peer-reviewed publications and regulatory submissions. The company is part of Roche.

providers.name: Iris Telehealth
providers.description: Iris Telehealth is an Austin, Texas telepsychiatry company, founded in 2013, that delivers virtual behavioral health care to healthcare organizations rather than direct to consumers. It contracts psychiatrists, psychiatric nurse practitioners, LCSWs and LPCs to hospitals and health systems, community mental health centers, community health centers and FQHCs, and Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics, covering pediatric through geriatric populations and low-acuity therapy through high-acuity psychiatry. Its service lines are Virtual Clinic (comprehensive care and behavioral health integration), On-Demand Services (24/7 emergency department psychiatry support), Scheduled Services (matched provider staffing), Bridge Clinic, and Iris Insights, an AI-enabled behavioral health analytics platform covering risk optimization, capacity management, a behavioral health command center and revenue cycle analytics. The company reports over 430 clinicians and over 210 partner organizations, and has been accredited by the Joint Commission for behavioral health care since 2019, earning recertification since. Its delivery model is deliberately technology-agnostic: Iris clinicians work inside each partner's existing EMR/EHR and e-prescribing tools over HIPAA-compliant video, so the integration burden sits with the partner's systems. Iris Telehealth publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contract, and operates no public GitHub organization.

providers.name: MicroTech Medical
providers.description: MicroTech Medical (Hangzhou) develops user-friendly diabetes glucose monitoring devices — blood glucose monitoring systems (BGMS), the AiDEX continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system, the Equil patch insulin pump, a closed-loop artificial pancreas, point-of-care testing (POCT), and LinX. Its AiDEX API Platform (aidexapi.microtechmd.com) is a self-service developer portal that registers developers and issues API credentials for accessing blood glucose data resources from AiDEX CGM devices, with separate global and China regional endpoints. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: SAVA
providers.description: SAVA (sava.health) is a health-monitoring company developing a minimally invasive, continuous multi-molecule biosensor worn just beneath the skin. The platform is designed to capture real-time molecular data - glucose, lactate, ketones, sodium, histamine, urea, alcohol, and cortisol - and surface it through a connected mobile app, aiming to shift healthcare toward preventative monitoring and personal wellness. The company is early stage and pre-launch, operating a waiting-list model for early access to its device rather than a public product. It publishes no first-party developer API or health-data API; its marketing site is built on Wix and exposes the Wix Site MCP endpoint and a published llms.txt for agentic access to public site content only. Backed by Balderton Capital.

providers.name: Ataraxis
providers.description: Ataraxis AI is a precision-medicine company building clinical AI foundation models that make disease predictable, beginning with oncology. Founded in 2022 by Jan Witowski, MD, PhD, and Krzysztof Geras, PhD (both formerly of NYU), Ataraxis trains multi-modal AI on hundreds of millions of pathology images to assess disease aggressiveness and predict cancer recurrence, treatment response, and survival. Its first product, Ataraxis Breast, is an AI-native, clinically validated prognostic and predictive test suite for breast cancer (Recurrence Risk, Chemotherapy Benefit, and Neoadjuvant Response) delivering same-day results without exhausting physical tissue. The company is backed by Obvious Ventures, AIX Ventures, and Giant Ventures, and advised by Turing Award winner Yann LeCun. Ataraxis operates a clinician portal rather than a public developer API; this profile captures its public identity, legal, and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: AvoMD
providers.description: AvoMD (Avo) is a clinical AI platform that integrates directly with electronic health record (EHR) systems to power AI copilots for healthcare workflows. It combines EHR data with trusted clinical knowledge bases to support decision-making, documentation, and care delivery across inpatient and outpatient settings. Avo's product line includes Chart Assist, an AI Scribe for ambient clinical documentation, and AI Consult, serving rural and small hospitals, large and mid-size hospitals, and ambulatory care, in partnership with medical societies and knowledge partners. The company is SOC 2 Type II compliant and backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: City Block
providers.description: Cityblock Health is a value-based healthcare provider delivering integrated primary care, behavioral health, and social-services support to Medicaid and lower-income (dual-eligible) Medicare populations across multiple U.S. markets. Cityblock pairs community-based care teams with a proprietary care-delivery technology platform to coordinate wraparound care for historically underserved communities. The company is backed by 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio profile; it operates as a care provider and does not publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Geneoscopy
providers.description: Geneoscopy is a commercial-stage molecular diagnostics company headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri, focused on gastrointestinal health. Its platform analyzes stool-derived eukaryotic RNA (seRNA) biomarkers, a proprietary approach the company applies to colorectal cancer screening, inflammatory bowel disease and other gastrointestinal conditions. Its lead product, ColoSense, is a noninvasive multi-target stool RNA (mt-sRNA) colorectal cancer screening test approved by the FDA in May 2024 for adults aged 45 and older at average risk; it evaluates eight colorectal neoplasia-associated RNA markers together with occult hemoglobin, and has since been added to the American Cancer Society and NCCN colorectal cancer screening guidelines. Geneoscopy operates a CLIA-certified (26D2253457) and CAP-accredited clinical laboratory with permits in New York, California, Maryland, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island and the District of Columbia, and partners with biopharma and research organizations on stool-biomarker diagnostics and prognostics. Geneoscopy is a diagnostics and clinical-laboratory company; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Leona
providers.description: Leona is a healthcare communication company building an AI co-pilot for doctors and medical teams who run their practices over WhatsApp. Patients keep messaging WhatsApp as they always have, while the clinician side moves into Leona, where work conversations are separated from personal ones, categorized and prioritized, summarized for context, and voice notes are transcribed. Teams delegate chats by role, keep internal notes on a patient that the patient never sees, and reuse templates for repeated answers. Founded by Caroline Merin (CEO, formerly COO at Rappi), Tom Chokel (CTO, formerly CTO at Modern Fertility) and Arela Solis (Head of Operations), Leona launched publicly in December 2025 and serves physicians across Latin America. It ships as iOS, Android and web clients and publishes no public developer API, SDKs or developer portal.

providers.name: Lumeon
providers.description: Lumeon is a clinical automation and care orchestration platform that uses intelligent automation and real-time data integration to remove inefficiencies from care-coordination processes. It lets health systems scale best-practice care pathways across the enterprise so clinicians can focus on patients while operational cost falls and outcomes improve. Lumeon serves 70+ health systems globally — including Optum, NYC Health+Hospitals, and the NHS — and is now part of Health Catalyst. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface is published; this profile captures the company identity and its security and compliance posture.

providers.name: Thyrocare
providers.description: Thyrocare Technologies Limited is an Indian chain of diagnostic and preventive-care laboratories headquartered in Navi Mumbai, founded in 1996. Built around a centralized, highly automated laboratory model, it focuses on affordable preventive health checkups, thyroid and pathology testing, and sells through a nationwide network of DSA (Direct Selling Agent) franchise partners. Norwest Venture Partners invested pre-IPO, and PharmEasy (API Holdings) acquired a majority stake in 2021. Its partner order-booking API (TechSo/BTS) is gated behind the DSA program and publishes no public OpenAPI.

providers.name: Tryadonis
providers.description: Adonis (Adonis Technology, Inc., tryadonis.com redirects to adonis.io) is a healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM) software company that applies AI to medical billing. Its platform connects in real time with a practice's existing EHR, practice-management, billing, and patient-portal systems to surface revenue-related insights, automate claims and billing workflows, and reduce manual work for revenue teams. The company is backed by Homebrew. This is a B2B SaaS product with a private, authenticated product API (api.adonis.io) and a customer app (app.adonis.io); it does not currently operate a public developer program, OpenAPI documentation, or API portal.

providers.name: WellTheory
providers.description: WellTheory is a virtual autoimmune care platform that provides whole-person support for people living with autoimmune and inflammatory conditions, pairing members with a dedicated care team for nutrition, lifestyle, and clinical guidance across more than 100 conditions. The company sells to employers and health plans as a covered benefit as well as direct to consumers, and is backed by Accel and General Catalyst. WellTheory publishes no public developer API surface today; its api.welltheory.com backend and docs are private/internal.

providers.name: Impress
providers.description: Impress (legal entity Smile2Impress SL) is a Barcelona-founded chain of clear-aligner orthodontic clinics, launched in 2019 by Vladimir Lupenko, Diliara Lupenko and Dr. Khaled Kasem, and today Europe's largest invisible-orthodontics clinic network. It runs 110+ doctor-led clinics across ten countries — Spain, Italy, Portugal, France, the United Kingdom, Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden, Ukraine and the United States — has treated more than 500,000 patients, and pairs in-clinic 3D intraoral scanning and patented diagnostics with AI-assisted treatment planning and remote monitoring through its patient mobile app. Impress publishes no developer portal, API reference, SDK, CLI, status page, changelog or machine-readable specification of any kind: contract discovery found no OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL SDL, AsyncAPI, MCP server, A2A agent card or .well-known document on any host it operates. Its one API host, api.smile2impress.com, is the private backend for the Impress patient app and the Impress Clinics practitioner app; it resolves and is live but answers HTTP 403 to every anonymous request, including every spec and .well-known path probed. Its GitHub organization, github.com/smile2impress, is real but carries only internal engineering tooling — five forks of Node.js/TypeScript infrastructure libraries and one first-party static-analysis tool, fe-explorer — and no client library for any Impress service. Products sold are orthodontic treatment, retainers and teeth whitening, priced and booked through the consumer site.

providers.name: La Fraise Pro
providers.description: La Fraise (LA FRAISE PRO SAS) is a French SaaS platform that digitizes the administrative patient journey for dental practices and dental centers: interactive treatment quotes (devis), patient-education video, informed consent, mutual-insurer coverage requests, and compliant electronic signature, all handled remotely. The product integrates natively with the French dental practice-management market — LOGOSw, Julie, Veasy, CS Trophy, Visiodent, Ardion, WeClever, Desmos, Galaxie and Effigie — with real-time bidirectional sync for LOGOSw, Veasy and Desmos. More than 3,500 dentists are equipped. Patient data is hosted on HDS-certified AWS infrastructure in the European Union, in line with article L.1111-8 of the French Code de la sante publique, and electronic signature follows Agence du Numerique en Sante (ANS) norms. La Fraise publishes no public developer API; practice-management integrations are provisioned by its own technical team.

providers.name: MedThread
providers.description: MedThread is an AI-powered Health Information Management (HIM) platform built specifically for long-term and post-acute care facilities — skilled nursing facilities (SNFs), nursing homes, assisted living facilities (ALFs), and rehabilitation centers. The platform digitizes paper records with AI-powered scanning, runs continuous automated audits for documentation completeness and regulatory compliance, monitors CMS quality metrics (rehospitalization, pressure ulcers, antipsychotic use), and provides a compliance dashboard, provider portal, and patient-facing Personal Health Record (PHR). MedThread advertises FHIR compatibility and pre-built EHR integrations (Epic, Cerner, Allscripts, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, Meditech, athenahealth, Greenway, Practice Fusion) via a secure API. Techstars-backed and based in Miami, FL. No public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI specification is published at this time.

providers.name: Spring Health
providers.description: Spring Health is a New York City-based digital mental health company that sells a comprehensive mental healthcare benefit to employers, health plans, brokers, channel partners, and healthcare providers. Its platform combines a clinically validated assessment, AI-driven matching, and a curated provider network to deliver therapy, medication management, coaching, an Employee Assistance Program (EAP), critical-incident response, work-life services, and self-guided digital exercises through a unified member experience branded Spring Life. For health plans and providers, Spring Health offers Springworks — its enterprise care-coordination and care-management offering — alongside a generative-AI member-facing assistant called Guide and clinician-facing AI tooling. Customers include General Mills, Hearst, and Moda Health, and the company publishes outcomes, research, and ROI evidence on long-term cost savings of mental health benefits. Spring Health operates as a B2B2C benefit: it does not expose a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documented HTTP API. Integrations with HRIS, SSO, eligibility files, and health-plan partners are delivered through enterprise implementation rather than a self-service API, and its GitHub organization (github.com/SpringHealth) has no public repositories.

providers.name: Sword Health
providers.description: Sword Health is a digital musculoskeletal (MSK) and virtual physical-therapy company that pairs licensed clinicians with an AI Care platform (programs including Thrive for MSK, Bloom for pelvic and women's health, Move, and Mind for mental health, with the Phoenix AI care specialist and the Sword Intelligence division). Founded in Portugal in 2015, it sells to employers, health plans, and governments rather than to individual developers. As of this enrichment pass Sword Health publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; its digital surface is member/clinician apps and employer client portals. Real public surfaces captured here are its trust center (SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR), legal pages, newsroom, and domain security posture.

providers.name: Axtria
providers.description: Axtria is an AI-first cloud software and data analytics company built for the life sciences industry, founded in 2010 and headquartered in Berkeley Heights, New Jersey. Its cloud product suite — Axtria DataMAx (AI-driven data management), Axtria InsightsMAx.ai (agentic AI and cloud analytics), Axtria SalesIQ (sales planning and operations), Axtria MarketingIQ (marketing analytics and omnichannel measurement) and Axtria CustomerIQ (omnichannel customer engagement) — helps pharmaceutical, biotech, medical device, animal health and consumer health commercial teams turn data into targeting, segmentation, incentive compensation, field force and brand decisions. Axtria reports 3,600+ employees serving 100+ life sciences companies, including 16+ of the top 20 pharmaceutical enterprises. Axtria publishes no public developer portal and no open API documentation: the product documentation host docs.axtria.com is HTTP Basic-auth gated to customers, and platform integration (Veeva CRM, Salesforce, Marketo and 20+ structured and unstructured life sciences data sources over SFTP and APIs) is delivered under enterprise contract rather than through a self-service developer surface.

providers.name: Bioniq
providers.description: Bioniq is a personalized nutrition and supplement company founded in London in 2019 that combines individual biomarker and blood-test data with a proprietary algorithm to formulate customized vitamin and mineral blends delivered as Swiss-made granules. Its consumer product line spans Bioniq GO (wellness-assessment based), Bioniq PRO (blood-test driven), and Bioniq Essential, supported by iOS and Android apps for tracking health and supplement routines. Bioniq is a portfolio company of HV Capital and now operates within Herbalife. It exposes consumer web, mobile, and partner/affiliate surfaces but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Careship
providers.description: Careship (operated by Care Companion GmbH, Berlin) is a German senior-care marketplace that connects elderly people and their families with vetted, non-medical everyday helpers ("Alltagshilfen") from their own neighborhoods. The platform covers companionship, shopping, household support, mobility and leisure, light personal care, and dementia support, and helps families finance care through statutory long-term care insurance (Pflegekasse). Careship operates across 20+ German cities including Berlin, Hamburg, Munich, Cologne, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, and Dresden. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Creandum; it is a consumer care-services business with no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Cerebral
providers.description: Cerebral is an American telehealth company providing online mental health and wellness care, including therapy, counseling, psychiatric evaluations, and medication management delivered through its website and mobile app on a subscription basis. Founded in 2020 by Kyle Robertson and Ho Anh, the company treats conditions such as depression, anxiety, insomnia, ADHD, and substance use disorder. Cerebral is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2, which led a $300M Series C in December 2021 valuing the company at roughly $4.8B. Cerebral is a direct-to-consumer product and does not publish a public developer API or programmatic surface; this API Evangelist profile tracks its public company and website properties.

providers.name: Chinese Medicine Online
providers.description: Chinese Medicine Online (中医在线) is a Beijing-based traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) continuing-education and academic-exchange platform, founded in 2015 and operated by Beijing Universe In Nutshell Technology Co., Ltd. (北京果壳宇宙教育科技有限公司) on behalf of the Beijing TCM Online Education Center (北京中医在线教育中心). Through its web platform at tcmmooc.com and its iOS/Android app, it publishes recorded and live video continuing-education courses from national TCM masters and senior practitioners, runs the 经方学社 (Classical Formulas Society) learning community and 精医社 membership, livestreams academic conferences, and sells course material through a paid knowledge marketplace. The company states a catalogue of roughly 19,600 courses from 3,900+ TCM experts and around 4 million registered users, the majority of them licensed practitioners. It has since extended into AI and SaaS for grassroots clinics, including the "Yi Yin" (伊尹) TCM classical-reasoning large language model launched in Songxian, Henan in September 2025, and clinic workflow tooling (prescription, patient and follow-up management). The platform is delivered strictly as an end-user web and mobile product — it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Dawaai
providers.description: Dawaai is Pakistan's leading digital healthcare platform, operating a licensed online pharmacy alongside telehealth and diagnostic services. Founded on a licensed retail pharmacy (License #1265, 2014) and headquartered in Karachi, Dawaai lets patients order authentic prescription and OTC medicines for temperature-controlled doorstep delivery, book doctor and mental-health consultations, order home-based lab tests and checkups, arrange home nursing and medical services, and subscribe to chronic-care programs for diabetes and obesity. It is a LegitScript-certified healthcare merchant that sources directly from manufacturers and distributors, with qualified pharmacists handling procurement, storage, and dispensing. Dawaai is backed by 500 Global and operates across Pakistan, including Karachi and Rawalpindi. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network via the venture portfolio pipeline; Dawaai publishes no public developer/API program at this time.

providers.name: Dawn
providers.description: Dawn (Sleepedy, Inc. dba Dawn) is a digital-health company offering a clinician-guided Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) program delivered through a mobile app. The service pairs users with licensed sleep coaches and therapists for weekly video sessions and between-session chat, daily 5-7 minute sleep lessons, live sleep-performance insights, and weekly progress reports, with the goal of treating primary and chronic insomnia and reducing reliance on sleep medication. Dawn is in-network with major U.S. insurers (Aetna, Anthem, Cigna, United Healthcare, Blue Cross Blue Shield) and offers an employer/enterprise workplace-wellness program. Backed by Kindred Ventures. Dawn publishes a consumer app and marketing site but no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Ezra
providers.description: Ezra (Ezra AI, Inc.) is a preventive-health company offering full-body MRI and CT cancer-screening scans directly to consumers. Its screening service scans up to 13 organs in as little as 22 minutes to detect early signs of cancer and hundreds of other conditions without harmful radiation, with plans spanning a full-body MRI, MRI with spine, a comprehensive skeletal/neurological MRI, and heart and lung CT scans, plus couples pricing and locations across the United States. Ezra was surfaced as a portfolio company of Seedcamp; this profile is a consumer healthcare company with no public developer API, and was enriched via the API Evangelist pipeline against its public web surface.

providers.name: Five Lives
providers.description: Five Lives is a health-technology company building evidence-based digital tools for dementia prevention and brain health for adults aged 50 and over. Founded by former Peak brain-training leaders Xavier Louis (CEO) and Sylvain Piquet (COO), the fully remote company operates two consumer mobile apps: Five Lives Brain Health, a prevention app available since 2021 with cognitive tests, brain games, and lifestyle tracking across five pillars (nutrition, sleep, physical activity, mood and social connection, and mental stimulation); and Five Lives Care, an evidence-based memory and autonomy programme for people aged 60+ launched in January 2026 and developed with leading memory centres in the UK and France. Its work draws on the FINGER study and the Lancet Commission's modifiable dementia risk factors, with research partners including the University of Oxford, Trinity College Dublin, the FINGER Brain Health Institute, Dementias Platform UK, and the Gerontopole d'Ile de France. Backed by Speedinvest. Five Lives does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Frontera
providers.description: Frontera (Frontera Health) is an AI-assisted clinical documentation company for behavioral health. Its software automates assessment and diagnosis report writing for Board Certified Behavior Analysts (BCBAs) and clinical psychologists working in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) and autism care, cutting report time from 6-10 hours to 2-3 hours. The platform pairs a BCBA-trained AI Assessment Builder and Diagnosis Builder with digital phenotyping, and is delivered as a HIPAA-compliant web application (customer login at portal.fronterahealth.com) rather than a public API. Frontera is a venture-backed portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer and security surface; as of this pass Frontera publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or MCP server.

providers.name: Lindus Health
providers.description: Lindus Health is a next-generation contract research organization (CRO) that runs clinical trials end to end for biotech and pharmaceutical sponsors. It pairs Citrus, an AI-assisted trial operating system connecting patient identification through final data capture, with centralized patient identification and enrollment (AI-powered EHR querying, digital pre-screening, centralized patient support), flexible site models spanning site-based, hybrid and fully virtual delivery, and integrated clinical services from protocol design through database lock. Its platform surface covers EDC, eSource, ePRO/eCOA, eConsent and CTMS. The company operates across the US, UK and Europe with APAC partnerships, employs over 160 staff, and works in cardiometabolic, respiratory, psychiatry, women's health and dermatology. Commercial engagements are performance-based with milestone pricing. Lindus Health publishes no public developer API, developer portal or API documentation; its public technical footprint is two open-source CDISC clinical-data repositories.

providers.name: Medmonk
providers.description: Medmonk is a pharma market access platform that connects brand teams, healthcare providers, pharmacies, and patients on a single real-time infrastructure. It automates point-of-sale copay enrollment, benefit investigations, prior authorizations, financial assistance, hub workflows, and adherence tracking across specialty and rare-disease medications, reaching roughly 98% of U.S. pharmacy and buy/bill network connectivity. Medmonk states it exposes FHIR-compliant APIs to integrate with existing EHR, CRM, and pharmacy systems, and claims SOC 2, HIPAA, and GDPR compliance, though it publishes no public developer portal or API documentation. Founded in the Y Combinator W12 batch.

providers.name: Mindbloom
providers.description: Mindbloom is a direct-to-consumer telehealth company offering at-home ketamine-assisted therapy for anxiety, depression, and PTSD, combining psychiatric clinician oversight, guided therapeutic sessions, and peer support. Clients complete a psychiatric evaluation, receive either sublingual tablets or subcutaneous injectable treatments, and are supported through a structured program with monitoring and integration guidance. The company reports having facilitated over 200,000 ketamine therapy sessions. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found no public API, developer platform, or developer documentation — Mindbloom is a consumer healthcare service, not an API provider.

providers.name: Paradigm Health
providers.description: Paradigm Health is an AI-native clinical trial platform connecting biopharma sponsors with a research-ready provider network spanning roughly 2,100 care locations across the United States. Founded in 2021 and headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, the company operates infrastructure implemented at healthcare provider organizations to make clinical research part of routine care. Its Study Conduct platform captures data directly from electronic health records and other structured and unstructured sources, algorithmically evaluates FDA-defined data points in real time, and transmits the critical safety and efficacy signals needed for regulatory determinations to trial sponsors and the FDA. Paradigm serves both trial sponsors (protocol optimization, feasibility and site selection, patient identification and enrollment, data collection and delivery, post-approval evidence) and research sites. The company acquired Flatiron Health's Clinical Research business, announced a research collaboration with the U.S. FDA, and is backed by ARCH Venture Partners, General Catalyst, and GV. Paradigm currently exposes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures its identity, legal, and published security/compliance surface.

providers.name: Q Bio
providers.description: Q Bio is a Redwood City, California health-technology company offering the Q Exam and the Q Bio Health Dashboard, sold directly at its clinic and through enterprise partners. The Q Exam is a comprehensive preventive-health assessment that combines whole-body non-contrast MRI, 120+ blood biomarkers, analysis of 163 risk-relevant genes, wearable data, medical history, and board-certified physician review into a single longitudinal health baseline. Imaging is quantified by Constellation, the company's FDA-cleared AI image-analysis software that segments organs and measures anatomy, and results are stored in the Q Bio Health Dashboard for year-over-year comparison. Q Bio is a portfolio company of a16z. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API, documentation, or well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: The Helper Bees
providers.description: The Helper Bees is an Austin-based aging-in-place technology company that operates one connected platform linking benefits, in-home service providers, and support so older adults can safely age at home. Its products include Care Concierge human guidance, an Aging-in-Place Marketplace for OTC products and nonmedical services (home care, safety modifications, meals, transportation), the Helpful benefits card, digital invoicing and claims processing for home and facility care, and digital nurse eligibility assessments for long-term care insurance. The company runs one of the nation's largest networks of vetted in-home care agencies and sells to Long-Term Care Insurance, Medicare Advantage, and Medicaid plan administrators. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. The Helper Bees publishes member and provider applications (the api.thehelperbees.com app host, the myhomealign.com provider portal, and mobile apps) but does not currently expose a public developer program, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs.

providers.name: Valerie Health
providers.description: Valerie Health is an AI-powered front office platform for independent healthcare provider groups, automating referral management, fax and document classification and data extraction, appointment scheduling, and growth analytics on top of existing EMR and practice management systems. Founded by Pete Shalek and Nitin Joshi and backed by General Catalyst and Redpoint Ventures with a $30M Series A, the company operates as a HIPAA Business Associate for its provider customers and publishes a Vanta-hosted trust center, but does not currently publish a developer portal or public API documentation.

providers.name: Weekend Health (Found)
providers.description: Weekend Health, Inc. (operating as Found / Found Health) is a consumer telehealth company offering personalized, science-based weight-loss care, including GLP-1 and other obesity medications, clinician oversight, coaching, and habit-change support delivered direct-to-consumer and through employer and health-plan channels. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, documentation, or developer portal is published as of this enrichment pass; the profile carries the company identity plus a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Capim
providers.description: Capim is a Sao Paulo-based vertical SaaS and fintech company for the dental sector in Brazil, founded in 2021 by Marcelo Lutz and Roberto Biselli. Its platform pairs dental-clinic management software - appointment scheduling (Agenda Capim), digital patient records, and AI-driven patient reactivation - with embedded financial products: buy-now-pay-later patient financing (Financiamento Capim, up to 36 installments), direct-credit collections (Carne Capim), and an integrated card/PIX payment terminal (Maquininha Capim). Capim serves more than 6,000 dental clinics, has issued over R$450 million in credit, and raised a US$26.7M Series A co-led by Valor Capital and QED Investors. No public developer API or documentation surface is currently published.

providers.name: Caremessage
providers.description: CareMessage is a healthcare technology non-profit that operates one of the largest patient engagement platforms serving low-income and underserved populations across the United States. Since 2013 the platform has reached more than 20 million patients and is used by roughly 1 in 7 federally qualified health centers plus 200+ free clinics. Its products include 1:1 direct messaging, appointment lifecycle messaging, population outreach, health coaching, closed-loop referrals, Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) workflows, and Wellness Copilot, an AI-backed diabetes-management automation. CareMessage does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API reference; access to the platform is through its web application and a login-gated help center. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched from CareMessage's public web surface.

providers.name: Ennoble Care
providers.description: Ennoble Care is a physician-led home-based healthcare provider delivering primary care, palliative care, and hospice care to seniors in the comfort of their own homes. Founded to bring the doctor back to the housecall, the company offers in-home primary care and chronic disease management, post-acute care transitions, advance care planning, bereavement services, and respite care across 13 states and Washington, DC (Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Maryland, Missouri, New Jersey, New York, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Texas, and Virginia). Ennoble Care is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. This profile has been enriched by the API Evangelist network; Ennoble Care is a healthcare-services company and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: FIGS
providers.description: FIGS, Inc. (NYSE: FIGS) is a founder-led, direct-to-consumer healthcare apparel and lifestyle brand founded in 2013 by Heather Hasson and Trina Spear and headquartered in Santa Monica, California. FIGS designs and sells premium scrubwear and non-scrubwear offerings — lab coats, underscrubs, outerwear, footwear, compression socks, loungewear, and accessories — directly to healthcare professionals through its Shopify-based online store at wearfigs.com. FIGS is a consumer e-commerce and retail brand with a customer help center and investor-relations presence; it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: heva
providers.description: heva is an AI-native healthcare and medical-tourism platform that connects patients with vetted medical practices, specialists, and providers across borders, with an initial focus on Spanish-speaking markets. The platform offers practice discovery by specialty and location, deposit-based online appointment booking, a conversational AI booking assistant (Heva AI), an online store for purchasing procedures and services, and secure payments via Stripe. Provider-facing tools cover practice management, patient acquisition, communications, and appointment coordination, delivered through the web and native iOS and Android provider apps. heva is a Techstars-backed company building "care without borders."

providers.name: Natural Cycles
providers.description: Natural Cycles is a Swedish women's-health company behind the first birth-control application cleared by the US FDA (2018) and CE-marked in Europe as a Class IIb medical device. Its subscription app uses a proprietary temperature-based algorithm to identify fertile and non-fertile days from a user's daily basal body temperature, supporting both preventing and planning pregnancy as well as cycle, ovulation, and perimenopause tracking. Temperature is captured with a paired Bluetooth basal thermometer or through consumer wearables the app integrates with — Apple Watch, Oura Ring, and the NC B1 band. Natural Cycles publishes clinical research, an educational content library (CycleMatters), an e-commerce shop for thermometers and tests, and a public bug-bounty / responsible-disclosure program, but it does not expose a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI. Backed by EQT Ventures.

providers.name: Nonnatech
providers.description: Nonnatech is a New York-based remote patient monitoring (RPM) and virtual health company that provides HIPAA-secured technology and clinical services for healthcare providers. Its platform integrates biometric sensors and passive home devices to deliver real-time analytics, chronic condition management, and population health programs across hospitals, health systems, physician practices, payers, ACOs, home care, long-term care, and senior living communities. Nonnatech offers turnkey device ordering, EHR data integration, and optional clinical monitoring, with no upfront costs to providers and roughly 30-day implementation. Nonnatech is a 500 Global portfolio company. It does not publish a public developer program, API documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Ro
providers.description: Ro (ro.co) is a direct-to-consumer telehealth company that connects patients with US-licensed healthcare providers entirely online, offering prescription treatment, provider visits, and pharmacy fulfillment across categories including men's and women's health, weight management (Ro Body), dermatology (Ro Derm), hair loss, fertility (Ro Fertility), and sexual health. Ro deliberately operates a "Zero-API" vertically integrated online-visit experience and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; its only public machine-readable surface is a security posture (RFC 9116 security.txt and a HackerOne vulnerability disclosure program). Ro is backed by Canaan Partners, General Catalyst, and Initialized Capital.

providers.name: Solv Health
providers.description: Solv Health operates a consumer marketplace (solvhealth.com and the Solv app) for booking same-day urgent care, primary care, and lab appointments, plus a provider-facing platform (scheduling, intake, patient acquisition, reputation management, messaging, payments) sold to clinics and health systems. There is no self-serve public developer API or published API reference on solvhealth.com; API access is gated behind a sales-led partnership. Solv states it exposes "interoperable APIs" that power custom booking experiences on partner websites and apps, a "Final Mile" API/network that lets digital-first and virtual-care partners (e.g. Included Health) hand patients off to real-time same-day appointment availability at Solv's national network of urgent care clinics, and bidirectional EHR interoperability (APIs, HL7, FHIR, and RPA) that syncs patient demographics, appointment status, and documents with systems like Epic, Athena, Cerner, Allscripts, DrChrono, eClinicalWorks, Experity, and NextGen. None of these capabilities have a published base URL, endpoint reference, or self-serve API key signup; access is provisioned per partner/clinic inside a commercial contract.

providers.name: Sondermind
providers.description: SonderMind is a Denver-based mental health company operating a measurement-based behavioral healthcare platform that connects people to licensed therapists and psychiatrists who have availability, accept insurance, and specialize in their needs. It offers virtual and in-person therapy and psychiatry across all 50 U.S. states, along with enterprise offerings for health systems, physician practices, payers, and Veterans. SonderMind is a General Catalyst portfolio company. As of this profile it publishes a consumer and clinician web platform (with a member/provider sign-in at api.sondermind.com) but no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; this repository tracks SonderMind's public web, content, and identity surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: AllCare
providers.description: AllCare is a Philippines-based digital employee-benefits and healthcare membership platform for freelancers and small-to-medium enterprises. It aggregates worker benefits that individuals and small teams would otherwise struggle to access, bundling HMO coverage, group life insurance, 24/7 teleconsultation, dental and optical care, mental-health counseling, annual physical exams, and productivity perks into flat-rate membership packages. Its SME Benefits Package is sold on an annual per-employee basis (minimum five employees) and is managed through a web dashboard for enrollment, member management, and benefit utilization. AllCare is a portfolio company of 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a healthcare/insurtech company profile.

providers.name: Forus (fka Tandem Health)
providers.description: Forus (formerly Tandem Health) is a US healthcare technology company building an AI-powered network that connects doctors, pharmacies, payers, and biopharma to bring new therapies to patients. Its platform automates the medication-access workflow end to end: prior authorization submissions, appeal-letter generation, insurance enrollment forms, benefit verification, pharmacy routing, patient status communication, PA renewal tracking, and affordability-program enrollment. It integrates with major EHRs so prescribers can submit directly, covers any drug/plan/pharmacy across all 50 states, and is HIPAA-compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified. The company publishes an engineering blog at build.forus.com but does not currently expose a public developer API. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures.

providers.name: Galileo
providers.description: Galileo (galileo.io, formerly reached at galileohealth.com) is a value-based, digitally enabled healthcare delivery company founded by Tom X. Lee (previously Epocrates and One Medical). It delivers 24/7 primary and multi-specialty care through a mobile app, in-home visits, mobile clinics, and virtual care, combining a proprietary clinical technology platform, a recruited network of primary-care and specialist clinicians, and hospitality-style member support. Galileo operates a fully bilingual (English/Spanish) platform and serves individuals and families, employers, small businesses, and health plans through membership and population- health partnerships. It is a care-delivery business, not an API platform: as of this profile Galileo publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Nitra
providers.description: Nitra is an integrated financial and operational platform — an "operating system" — for independent medical practices, unifying business banking, spend management, payments, accounting, capital, and front-desk automation in one system. Its core products include the Nitra Card (a Visa business card with cashback and vendor pricing), NitraMart (a medical-supplies marketplace), BillPay payment processing, accounting integrations (QuickBooks, Nextech), Trina (an AI assistant for phone reception and invoice matching), and capital products such as lending, equipment financing, and insurance factoring. Nitra primarily serves eye care, aesthetics, dental specialty, and fertility practices as well as multi-site groups. The company is SOC 2 Type II certified and HIPAA-aware, holds funds at FDIC-insured banks, and is backed by a16z and Pantera Capital. Nitra publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Nova Benefits
providers.description: Nova Benefits is an India-based employee health and benefits platform that provides group health insurance, super top-up plans, and COVID-19 cover alongside wellness services such as telehealth consultations, mental-wellness support, fitness programs, maternity benefits, and annual health, dental and vision checkups. It gives HR teams an employer dashboard for administering benefits and managing claims, and gives employees web and mobile (iOS/Android) apps to view coverage, book consultations, and file and track claims. The company reports serving 500+ companies covering 200,000+ employees, is ISO 27001:2022 certified and SOC 2 Type II compliant, and operates as an IRDAI-regulated insurance broker. Nova Benefits publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: OneHealthCompany
providers.description: The One Health Company is a Palo Alto veterinary precision-oncology company, best known for its FidoCure platform, that brings human-grade precision cancer medicine to dogs. FidoCure sequences a dog's tumor with next-generation DNA sequencing, matches the cancer-driving mutations to targeted therapies, and gives veterinarians an individualized treatment plan grounded in the world's largest proprietary canine cancer dataset (billions of data points across a network of more than 1,300 veterinary clinics). The company was founded in 2015 by Christina Lopes and Ben Lewis on the "One Health" thesis that treating cancer in companion dogs also advances real-world evidence for human oncology. It is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z bio), Y Combinator, Polaris Partners, Borealis Ventures, Lerer Hippeau and Tau Ventures. As of this profile the company exposes a consumer and veterinarian web experience (including a veterinarian login portal) but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or programmatic surface.

providers.name: Science
providers.description: Science Corporation is a clinical-stage medical technology company founded in 2021 by Max Hodak and headquartered in Alameda, California, with offices in Research Triangle Park, North Carolina and Paris, France. Science develops brain-computer interface (BCI) and neural-engineering technologies to restore vision, cognition, and mobility, including the PRIMA retinal implant for patients with macular degeneration, the Biohybrid neural interface, and the Vessel perfusion platform. Through its Foundry division Science also offers MEMS production and neural-engineering services to external partners. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Science publishes no public web API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

providers.name: Sofía
providers.description: Sofía is a 100% Mexican health insurance company (aseguradora) offering medical coverage for individuals, families, and businesses, delivered primarily through a mobile app with plans that carry no deductibles. Regulated in Mexico by the CNSF, Secretaría de Salud, and CONDUSEF, and backed by Index Ventures. This is a consumer/enterprise insurance provider surfaced as a portfolio-company lead; a live probe of the public surface found no developer program, API, or /.well-known/ discovery documents, so this profile remains identity-only pending any future API exposure.

providers.name: Sonar Mental Health
providers.description: Sonar Mental Health provides 24/7 text-based wellbeing coaching and care navigation for youth. Trained Wellbeing Coaches lead the conversations, supported by AI tooling that surfaces context and flags risk without making independent decisions, delivering between-visit and after-hours support, escalation and care coordination to higher levels of care, and real-time insights dashboards for measurement-based care across schools, health systems, primary care, and EAP pathways. The company reports serving 20,000+ young people with higher engagement between visits, and is backed by 500 Global. There is no public developer API surface; this profile captures the company's identity, security posture (SOC 2, HIPAA), and public web properties.

providers.name: Casana
providers.description: Casana (Casana Care) is a Rochester, New York digital-health company building passive, in-home remote patient monitoring hardware. Its flagship Smart Seat (formerly the Heart Seat) is a toilet-seat replacement that captures vital signs — heart rate, heart-rate variability, blood-oxygen (SpO2), respiration rate, blood-pressure insights, and sit-to-stand power — during normal bathroom use, with no wearables, no daily charging, and explicitly no camera or microphone. Readings sync to companion iOS, Android, and web apps for patients, families, and caregivers. The company operates in the digital health, remote patient monitoring, and connected medical-device space and is backed by General Catalyst and Kaiser Permanente. As of this profile Casana publishes a consumer product, companion apps, and legal/privacy pages, but no public developer program, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Cooler Heads
providers.description: Cooler Heads Care, Inc. is a San Diego medical device company founded in 2018 by Kate Dilligan that makes Amma, an FDA-cleared Portable Scalp Cooling System (PSCS) used to reduce chemotherapy-induced hair loss. Amma circulates chilled fluid through a fitted cap to constrict scalp blood vessels and limit chemotherapy delivery to hair follicles, and is designed to be portable enough that patients can keep cooling outside the infusion chair. The company sells to infusion centers and oncology practices and publishes patient, provider, reimbursement and training material on its own site. It ships no developer API, SDK or public API documentation; its only machine-readable public surface is the Wix-platform site MCP endpoint and llms.txt served from its own host.

providers.name: Svastia
providers.description: Svastia (Svastia Genetics Inc.) is a precision-genomics and oncology data company that bundles clinical research products with cutting-edge bioinformatics to accelerate precision cancer therapy. It offers DNA/RNA sequencing, exome and gene-panel assays, immune (B/T-cell) repertoire sequencing, cell-based drug-efficacy screening, therapeutic-antibody development toolkits, and siRNA design, together with biomarker analytics (Tumor Mutational Burden, Microsatellite Instability) and clinical reporting based on ACMG/ASCO guidelines. Svastia serves hospitals, diagnostics labs, researchers, and CROs, and runs a bespoke clinical/genetic data-collection service across a hospital network, with HL7-FHIR data exchange between EHR and Clinical Trial Management Systems. Products are delivered through a login-gated web portal; the company does not publish a public developer API. Backed by 500 Global; offices in San Francisco (USA) and Cambridge (UK).

providers.name: Amperos Health
providers.description: Amperos Health (Amperos) is an AI-native insurance revenue recovery platform for healthcare providers. It uses agentic AI together with experienced revenue cycle management (RCM) specialists to run the full insurance collections process, from claim submission through denial resolution to payment. The platform automates first-touch routine tasks, works complex denials with specialist oversight, and adapts configurable workflows to each organization's procedures across specialties including orthopedics, cardiology, behavioral health, DME/HME, ophthalmology, anesthesiology, dermatology, urology, dental, and oncology. Amperos reports outcomes such as higher claim recovery, reduced accounts receivable backlogs, and lower cost to collect for the healthcare providers it serves. The company is backed by Uncork Capital and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio company. Amperos currently exposes a marketing and demo-request surface rather than a public developer API; this profile captures its public web properties and security posture.

providers.name: Chamber Cardio
providers.description: Chamber Cardio is a Washington, D.C.-based healthcare technology company building a cardiology-focused platform for value-based care. Chamber partners with cardiology practices and health plans to align clinical signals, workflows, and patient data so cardiologists can identify high-risk patients earlier, close gaps against treatment guidelines, and reduce administrative burden. Its workflow-integrated AI surfaces clearer signal from the large volumes of cardiovascular data generated in care, supporting better patient outcomes and financial predictability for payers as cardiology moves beyond fee-for-service. The company supports more than 500 cardiologists across seven states and raised a $60M Series A led by Frist Cressey Ventures, with participation from General Catalyst, AlleyCorp, American Family Ventures, Company Ventures, Optum Ventures, Healthworx Ventures, and Black Opal Ventures. Chamber does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation portal; its platform is built on a FHIR-based data stack (Medplum) with internal REST and GraphQL services.

providers.name: Virgin Pulse
providers.description: Virgin Pulse is a corporate health and employee wellbeing platform that in 2024 merged with HealthComp and rebranded as Personify Health, operating today at personifyhealth.com. The company delivers a personalized health platform that unites wellbeing, healthcare navigation and advocacy, benefits administration, third-party administration (TPA), and rewards into a single employee experience for enterprises, health plans, and health systems. Integration with Personify Health is handled through an authentication-gated developer portal (developer.personifyhealth.com) and a partner marketplace (marketplace.personifyhealth.com); there is no publicly documented, open API specification. This profile was seeded as an Insight Partners portfolio lead and enriched from the company's live public surface (llms.txt, status page, developer portal, and DNS/TLS probes).

providers.name: Allswell
providers.description: Allswell is an online mental health platform providing virtual, trauma-informed therapy for the LGBTQ+ community. Licensed therapists with master's degrees in social work, counseling, or marriage and family therapy deliver individual telehealth sessions alongside peer support groups and skills-building resources, covering trauma, anxiety, depression, identity exploration, and relationship dynamics. Allswell serves clients in Maryland, DC, and Virginia, accepting Medicaid and major insurance plans as well as cash-pay. Backed by Techstars, it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Amperos
providers.description: Amperos provides AI-powered insurance claims management and revenue recovery for healthcare providers, using agentic AI to recover insurance revenue end-to-end and drive more collections, faster. The platform automates denial management, claims processing, and collections workflows while keeping human experts in the loop for complex cases, and integrates with major EHR / practice-management systems including eClinicalWorks, Athenahealth, NextGen, Epic, ModMed, and Dentrix. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. Amperos exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface at this time; the product is delivered as a managed service and web application.

providers.name: AnswersNow
providers.description: AnswersNow is a virtual Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) therapy provider for individuals with autism, delivering personalized, evidence-based care from board-certified behavior analysts (BCBAs) through its proprietary telehealth platform. Families access one-on-one therapy sessions, caregiver and parent training, and individualized treatment plans remotely, expanding access to ABA care in areas with limited in-person availability. AnswersNow accepts major insurance carriers including Medicaid, is BHCOE accredited and a CASP member organization, and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company. This profile has been enriched with company identity and domain-security posture; AnswersNow publishes a consumer web application (web.getanswersnow.com) but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: August AI
providers.description: August AI is a consumer health-AI companion that helps people understand their symptoms, lab reports, prescriptions, and medications, and connects them to licensed physicians through asynchronous, chat-based telehealth visits. Founded in 2022 by Anuruddh Mishra after a four-month misdiagnosis, August operates as a 24/7 health assistant available on iOS, Android, and WhatsApp, storing lab reports and conversation history in long-term memory to deliver personalized guidance. The service pairs a free AI symptom-assessment experience with paid online doctor consultations from board-certified MDs licensed across all 50 US states. August reports serving millions of users across 160+ countries in 30+ languages, and publishes medical benchmarks including 100% accuracy on the USMLE, 97.4% on MedQA, 99.4% on lab-report document processing, and 100% precision/recall on emergency escalation. It is backed by Accel and Claypond Capital. August is a consumer application and does not currently publish a developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Cyberpsyc
providers.description: CyberPsyc Software Solutions, operating as WellTrack Boost (now part of ProtoCall Services), builds self-guided, clinically-supported digital cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) tools for behavioral health and wellness. The platform lets users assess and understand their mental health on their own devices and schedule through MoodCheck mood tracking, the Zen Room, a Thought Diary, an Activity Scheduler, Fun and Achievement planning, and guided modules for stress, anxiety, and depression. WellTrack Boost is deployed by college counseling centers and certified community behavioral health clinics, offering institutional single sign-on through a SAML integration surface. No public developer REST API or OpenAPI is currently published.

providers.name: Dorsata
providers.description: Dorsata is a women's health technology company based in Arlington, Virginia that reimagines the electronic health record (EHR) experience for obstetrics and gynecology providers, life sciences, and health plans. Its flagship Dorsata Prenatal platform overlays a practice's existing EHR with an ACOG-aligned prenatal flowsheet and a clinical rules engine that surfaces the right guidance at the right point of care, improving diagnosis, treatment, and documentation while reducing physician burnout. Additional products include Dorsata Insights, which gathers standardized real-world clinical data from women's health providers (including populations historically underrepresented in clinical studies), Dorsata Pathways, and an Adnexal Mass solution. The platform serves 300+ practice sites and thousands of clinical users across roughly 20 states, documenting hundreds of thousands of pregnancies. Dorsata raised a $5.2M Series A with participation from QED Investors, Women's Health USA, LabCorp, Fool Ventures, and Gore Range Capital. This API Evangelist profile tracks Dorsata as a healthtech company; the company exposes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: NOCD
providers.description: NOCD is a virtual mental-health provider specializing in the treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder. Through its web and mobile applications the company matches members with licensed therapists trained in Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) therapy, delivers live video sessions, and provides between-session messaging, a peer community, and in-app therapeutic tools. NOCD is in-network with a large number of US health plans and serves children, adolescents, and adults. The product is delivered as an end-user clinical service — the company operates a private mobile/web application backend at api.treatmyocd.com but publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Plenful
providers.description: Plenful is an AI-powered workflow automation platform for pharmacy and healthcare operations, founded in 2021 and headquartered in San Francisco with an office in New York City. The platform automates complex, high-ROI administrative pharmacy workflows — 340B audit and optimization, 340B referral capture, rebate and Maximum Fair Price (MFP) reconciliation, benefits verification and prior authorization, and infusion order intake — using large language models and machine learning tuned to each organization's data. It ingests PDFs, flat files, APIs, HL7 feeds, and databases, supports unlimited organizational logic rules, and serves 100+ healthcare organizations including Prisma Health, Renown Health, Temple Health, Cencora, and Samaritan Health Services. Plenful is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Notable Capital (formerly GGV Capital), SUSA Ventures, TQ Ventures, and Waterline Ventures. Plenful ships an enterprise SaaS product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Prosper Health
providers.description: Prosper Health is a telehealth provider focused exclusively on autistic and neurodivergent adults, offering virtual autism diagnostic assessments and ongoing affirming, strength-based therapy delivered by licensed psychologists and therapists who specialize in adult autism. Its adult-validated, telehealth-native assessment (an alternative to the child-oriented ADOS) runs entirely online across two psychologist sessions plus a feedback session, with results reported within roughly two weeks. Prosper Health accepts major insurers (Aetna, BCBS, Cigna, Oscar, Oxford, United) across 20-plus US states. It is a direct-to-consumer clinical care company with no public developer API surface; this profile tracks its web, security, and identity properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Rula
providers.description: Rula is a telehealth mental health platform that connects patients with licensed therapists and psychiatric providers who accept their insurance. Operating as an in-network behavioral health marketplace across all 50 states, Rula matches individuals with more than 23,000 licensed clinicians for individual, couples, family, child, and teen therapy as well as psychiatric medication management, covering 90+ conditions including anxiety, depression, ADHD, PTSD, OCD, and addiction. Rula is in-network with 120+ insurance plans nationwide (Aetna, Cigna, Optum, UnitedHealthcare, Blue Cross, Kaiser), with patients paying an average of about $15 per session with insurance. Rula publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or partner API surface as of this profile; care is delivered through its patient and provider web applications.

providers.name: Vocca Ai
