providers.description: Vocca is a healthcare voice-AI company (backed by Speedinvest) that builds AI voice and text agents acting as a 24/7 receptionist for medical groups and practices. Vocca handles inbound and outbound patient calls, appointment bookings, reminders, and follow-ups across specialties including imaging, dental, cardiology, gynecology, ophthalmology, anesthesiology, general medicine, hospitals, and multi-practice clinics, so clinical teams spend less time on admin and more time on care. The company operates a customer-facing product with French and English coverage; it does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification, so this profile carries company identity and website link-properties only.

providers.name: Amedisys
providers.description: Amedisys, Inc. is a United States home health, hospice, palliative and high-acuity in-home care company headquartered in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. Founded in 1982, it delivers skilled nursing, physical and occupational therapy, medical social work, hospice and palliative care through a nationwide network of care centers, and — through Contessa, an Amedisys company — hospital-level and skilled-nursing-level care delivered in the patient's home in partnership with health systems and payers. Formerly listed on Nasdaq as AMED, Amedisys was acquired by UnitedHealth Group's Optum in a $3.3 billion all-cash transaction that closed in August 2025 after a Department of Justice settlement requiring the divestiture of 164 home health and hospice locations; it continues to operate under the Amedisys brand. Amedisys publishes no public API: there is no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, gRPC or SOAP contract, no SDK on any package registry, no MCP server and no A2A agent card. Clinical data moves between Amedisys, its referral sources, its EHR vendors and payers under HIPAA business-associate agreements and bilateral integration contracts rather than through a documented public interface.

providers.name: Besoundbreast
providers.description: BeSound (Besoundbreast) is a women's-health technology platform offering modern, radiation-free breast imaging using ABUS ultrasound to help find cancers that mammograms can miss, particularly in women with dense breast tissue. BeSound connects patients with independent partner medical groups who deliver the imaging; results reach a secure patient portal within 24-48 weekday hours. Screening breast ultrasound is $349, with locations in Los Angeles (Melrose Ave) and Beverly Hills. BeSound is a consumer healthcare service and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and the machine-readable llms.txt it publishes for AI agents.

providers.name: Bodyport
providers.description: Bodyport is a San Francisco healthcare technology company delivering remote heart-failure monitoring. Its FDA-cleared Cardiac Scale captures hemodynamic biomarkers through a patient's feet in under 30 seconds and transmits the readings over cellular to care teams within minutes. The company's Congestion Index algorithm combines multiple hemodynamic biomarkers to detect worsening heart failure earlier than standard weight-based rules, and its connected Care Platform surfaces monitoring, alerts, and care coordination through a clinical dashboard and a patient portal. Bodyport works with health systems and pharma partners including Geisinger, Boehringer Ingelheim, Stanford, Brigham and Women's Hospital, Duke, and Yale. The company publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its product, portal, and compliance surfaces.

providers.name: Gyant
providers.description: Gyant was a San Francisco-based digital health company that built an AI-powered conversational virtual assistant for health systems, guiding patients through symptom checking, care navigation, and triage across web and messaging channels. In 2022 Gyant was acquired by Fabric (fabrichealth.com), and gyant.com now redirects to Fabric's healthcare care-access platform, which combines conversational AI with physician-built clinical protocols for virtual care, patient engagement, and clinical automation. Gyant does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures the company's identity, published legal/compliance surface, and domain security posture.

providers.name: Instride Health
providers.description: InStride Health is a virtual mental health provider delivering specialized, insurance-based treatment for children, teens, and young adults ages 7 to 24 who struggle with anxiety, OCD, panic, phobias, school avoidance, and related disorders. Its structured four-to-eight month program pairs each patient with a coordinated care team of a therapist, a psychiatric prescriber, and an exposure coach, combining evidence-based cognitive behavioral therapy and exposure-and-response prevention delivered over telehealth. The company is backed by General Catalyst and tracked in the API Evangelist network; it operates as a clinical care provider and publishes no public API, developer program, or SDK.

providers.name: Juniper Behavioral Health
providers.description: Juniper Behavioral Health (now operating as Camber, camber.health) is a healthcare revenue-cycle-management (RCM) software company for specialty and behavioral health providers. Founded in 2021 and backed by a16z, Y Combinator, and Craft Ventures, the company automates medical billing, claims processing, denial management, and payment analytics so behavioral and specialty clinicians (ABA, PT, ENT, allergy) can collect more from insurance and spend less time on administrative overhead. Their platform is built on AI systems trained on more than $2.5B in claims data. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched from the public Camber website; the company exposes a customer web application (app.camber.health) and a published responsible-disclosure policy but no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Somethings
providers.description: Somethings is a teen mental health support platform that connects adolescents with Certified Peer Specialist Mentors through a mobile app for iOS and Android. Rather than traditional therapy or AI chatbots, teens can call or chat anytime with trained mentors who have personal lived experience overcoming challenges like anxiety, depression, self-harm, eating disorders, and ADHD, backed by clinical supervision. The service is HIPAA-compliant and sold to health plans, insurers, employers, and directly to parents. Somethings is a venture-backed company in the API Evangelist network; it operates a consumer/clinical mobile product and does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: TrueCare24
providers.description: TrueCare24 is a nationwide care platform providing care professionals and services for home and business. Its offerings span in-home care, on-demand healthcare staffing, visiting nurses, behavioral health and counseling, and workplace health programs including flu vaccination, diabetes screening, and COVID-19 testing and vaccination services. A 500 Global portfolio company, TrueCare24 operates customer dashboards and a provider portal but publishes no public developer program or API.

providers.name: Vedanta Biosciences
providers.description: Vedanta Biosciences is a late clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered at 19 Blackstone Street in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded by PureTech Health together with a group of scientific co-founders who pioneered the modern understanding of cross-talk between the human microbiome and the immune system. The company develops a potential new category of oral Live Biotherapeutic Products built from rationally defined consortia of human commensal bacteria grown from pure clonal cell banks rather than donor-derived stool, and it maintains technical expertise in the manufacture of live organisms. Its lead program, VE303, is an eight-strain defined bacterial consortium in the global Phase 3 RESTORATiVE303 registrational study for the prevention of recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection, following Phase 2 results showing a greater than 80% reduction in the odds of CDI recurrence versus placebo; VE202 is in development for inflammatory bowel disease and VE707 for prevention of multidrug-resistant organism infections. Vedanta has raised a $68 million Series D and a $106.5 million financing, and its programs are supported by non-dilutive awards from BARDA and CARB-X. Vedanta is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it runs a WordPress marketing and corporate site, publishes no developer portal, no SDKs, no GitHub organization and no machine-readable API contract, and an August 2026 probe of vedantabio.com found no OpenAPI, no /llms.txt, no MCP endpoint, no A2A agent card and an empty /.well-known/ discovery surface.

providers.name: Bayer
providers.description: Bayer is a German multinational pharmaceutical and life sciences company operating across pharmaceuticals, consumer health, and crop science. Bayer does not publish a single corporate-level public developer portal; integration is delivered through enterprise partner programs, the Bayer Crop Science Climate FieldView ecosystem (partner-gated APIs and certified-partner integrations), pharmacovigilance and clinical-trial data exchange, and EDI / x12 channels with distributors and pharmacy benefit managers.

providers.name: Chi Longevity
providers.description: Chi Longevity is a Singapore-based longevity medicine and healthy-aging clinic that focuses on biological-age optimization rather than reactive medicine, built on The Maier Method developed by co-founder Professor Andrea Maier. The practice combines precision health mapping (blood panels, genetic and cognitive testing, cardiovascular and metabolic analysis), flagship and specialised longevity programmes, cognitive and physical training, a branded NMN supplement, and ongoing support through health coaching, physician and dietitian consultations, and a client portal. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer API is currently published, so this profile carries the company identity, domain-security posture, and published web properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Glass Health
providers.description: Glass Health is a San Francisco-based clinical AI company founded in 2021 by Dereck Paul (CEO) and Graham Ramsey (Head of Product) that builds an AI clinical decision support (CDS) and ambient scribing co-pilot for physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, residents, and medical students. The Glass platform combines large language model reasoning with curated, physician-reviewed clinical guidelines to generate ranked differential diagnoses, evidence-based assessment and plans, chart summaries, and direct answers to clinical questions ("Consult"), all delivered with inline citations. Glass also provides ambient scribing that listens during patient encounters and generates History and Physical notes, progress notes, discharge summaries, and patient-facing instructions, plus EHR integration via SMART on FHIR to pull demographics, problem lists, medications, laboratory values, vital signs, imaging, and encounter data into the workflow. Glass offers a tiered SaaS plan (Lite free tier, Starter at $20/month, Pro at $90/month, Max at $200/month) along with iOS and Android apps, and a public Glass Developer API ($250/month minimum, token-metered beyond the floor) that exposes the same clinical AI agent — Consult, Differential Diagnosis, Assessment and Plan, and Scribing endpoints — for third-party healthcare products. Glass is backed by Breyer Capital and graduated from Y Combinator's W23 batch, with roughly $6.5M in total disclosed funding. The provider does not publish an open OpenAPI specification or open-source SDKs; integration details are gated behind the developer portal and an enterprise contact at enterprise@glass.health.

providers.name: Medzoomer
providers.description: Medzoomer is an on-demand prescription delivery platform that connects pharmacies, healthcare providers, and patients through a secure, HIPAA-compliant network of verified couriers. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Tampa, Florida, the company handles last-mile medication logistics, including controlled substances (Schedule II-V), with tamper-evident packaging, FDA/TSA-approved envelopes, and real-time order tracking. Pharmacies and couriers operate through dedicated web and mobile applications, and the platform is backed by Techstars, UnitedHealthcare Accelerator, and other investors. Medzoomer operates a private pharmacy integration API but publishes no public developer documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Mend
providers.description: Mend is a HIPAA-compliant telehealth and patient engagement platform for mental and behavioral healthcare organizations, powering appointment scheduling, automated reminders, secure video visits, digital intake forms and consents, patient messaging, payments, and AI no-show prediction. Mend integrates with EHR and practice-management systems through a combination of HL7, SFTP, and an API served from api.mendfamily.com. That API exists and is used by Mend's own portal for session initialization and signaling, but its reference documentation is delivered through a login-gated customer knowledge base rather than a public developer portal, so Mend's programmatic surface is best characterized as partner- and customer-gated rather than openly self-serve.

providers.name: Min Doktor
providers.description: Min Doktor is a Swedish digital healthcare provider (operated by MD International AB) offering online primary care through its mobile app and web service. Founded in 2013 as one of Sweden's first digital-first care providers, it connects patients with doctors, psychologists and nurses for consultations, prescriptions, referrals and vaccinations, and also runs white-label care services for partners such as Skandia. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of EQT Ventures. Min Doktor operates as a consumer/patient-facing service and does not publish a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures its verifiable public security, identity and compliance footprint.

providers.name: Vertex Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Vertex Pharmaceuticals is a global biotechnology company headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, focused on scientific innovation to create transformative medicines for people with serious diseases. The company specializes in cystic fibrosis, sickle cell disease, beta thalassemia, APOL1-mediated kidney disease, pain, and other serious conditions. Vertex is committed to responsible sharing of clinical trial data with qualified researchers through formal data request processes.

providers.name: Watsi
providers.description: Watsi is a San Francisco-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit crowdfunding platform that lets donors directly fund surgeries and medical care for patients in low-income countries, working through vetted medical partners across Africa, Asia, and Latin America. Founded in 2011 and the first nonprofit funded by Y Combinator, Watsi has directed more than $20 million to patient healthcare. Watsi previously published a read-only JSON API at developers.watsi.org, but that developer portal and api.watsi.org no longer resolve, so no public API surface is currently available.

providers.name: WeiMai
providers.description: WeiMai (微脉) is a Chinese healthcare technology company operated by Choice Technology Inc. and headquartered in Hangzhou. It runs an internet-based medical services marketplace and licensed internet hospitals (including Hainan WeiMai Internet Hospital) that connect patients with doctors for online consultation, pharmaceutical products, medical devices, and health-management service packages, delivered primarily through the WeiMai consumer mobile app. WeiMai also operates a partner-facing Open Platform (微脉开发平台) at openapi.myweimai.com that exposes a Swagger 2.0 API surface for approved integrators; the public specification is a minimal stub with no operations exposed without partner credentials. The company is backed by IDG Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a healthcare portfolio company.

providers.name: AmplifyMD
providers.description: AmplifyMD is a virtual care platform for hospitals and health systems, providing a nationwide network of remote specialists across more than 15 essential fields. It powers telemedicine across emergent, inpatient, asynchronous, SNF/LTAC, virtual clinic, and direct-to-patient care models, and integrates with major EHR systems including Epic, Oracle Health, athenahealth, Allscripts, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, TruBridge, and MedHost to help organizations build sustainable clinical staffing models. Backed by Forerunner Ventures.

providers.name: Augmedix
providers.description: Augmedix is a San Francisco-based health technology company providing ambient AI medical documentation (AI scribe) services that capture patient-clinician conversations and generate clinical notes so that physicians can focus on patient care instead of EHR data entry. Founded in 2012, the company went public on Nasdaq in 2021 (AUGX) and was acquired by Commure in October 2024, becoming part of Commure's clinician-workflow platform alongside HCA Healthcare-aligned tooling. Augmedix's product line spans three service tiers — Augmedix Go (self-service AI scribe), Augmedix Assist (AI drafting with human editing, coding, and referral-letter support, notes ready within an hour), and Augmedix Live (full-service dedicated medical documentation specialist before, during, and after the visit) — plus specialty variants for Emergency Medicine, oncology, and other specialties. The platform integrates with major EHRs including Epic, Oracle Cerner, athenahealth, Meditech, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, and iKnowMed, and is HIPAA-compliant and HITRUST-certified. Augmedix's GitHub presence consists of internal QA, scribe-app base, and ambient API automation repositories; there is no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI specification — integration with Augmedix is handled through enterprise EHR partnerships and the Commure clinician platform rather than a self-service developer surface.

providers.name: Boston Heart Diagnostics (Eurofins Scientific)
providers.description: Boston Heart Diagnostics is a specialty cardiovascular diagnostics laboratory, part of Eurofins Scientific, that has been improving patient outcomes since 2007 through a combination of integrated diagnostics, advanced lipid and metabolic testing, genetic risk evaluation, personalized reporting, and a scientifically designed nutrition and lifestyle program. It serves clinicians and patients through a provider portal and a patient portal (mybostonheart.com) rather than a public developer API; there is no published developer portal, OpenAPI, or programmatic surface at this time. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the identity and security-posture fields below are captured from the provider's public web presence.

providers.name: C the Signs
providers.description: C the Signs is a London-based healthcare technology company, founded in 2016 by Dr Bea Bakshi and Dr Miles Payling, that uses artificial intelligence to help clinicians detect and refer patients at risk of cancer at the earliest, most treatable stage. Registered as an MHRA Class I medical device, its clinical decision support platform analyzes more than 1,000 validated, evidence-based data points across signs, symptoms and risk factors to recommend the right investigations or urgent referrals in under 60 seconds. The platform is used widely across the UK's NHS and health systems, has helped identify over 70,000 patients with cancer across 100+ cancer types at reported 99% sensitivity, and is backed by an $8M Series A investment from Khosla Ventures. It has no public developer API; this profile tracks the company as an API Evangelist network lead.

providers.name: Comprehensive Pharmacy Services
providers.description: Comprehensive Pharmacy Services, now operating as CPS Solutions, LLC, is a healthcare company with more than 50 years of experience providing pharmacy and hospital solutions across the care continuum. It serves independent hospitals, health systems, integrated delivery networks (IDNs), and specialized health facilities with specialty pharmacy, pharmacy management, telepharmacy (24/7/365 support), 340B program compliance, supply chain management, rehabilitation services, and consulting. The company operates two proprietary SaaS platforms — CPS Optimizer for pharmacy management and TherigySTM for specialty pharmacy management — supported by 2,500+ healthcare professionals serving 800+ customers across the United States and Puerto Rico. No public API or developer program is currently published; this profile captures the company identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Crossoverhealth
providers.description: Crossover Health is an advanced primary care provider that delivers integrated, team-based healthcare for employers and their members through its proprietary Care Platform. Its services span primary care, physical medicine, mental health, health coaching, care navigation, and occupational medicine, delivered through on-site and near-site health centers and a 50-state virtual provider network. Crossover Health is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification has been found on its web properties.

providers.name: Enable
providers.description: Enable Medicine is a healthcare and life-sciences data company that licenses an integrated, AI-ready index of clinical, spatial, cellular, and molecular data. Its research platform helps biopharma companies, academic institutions, and healthcare providers run spatial-biology analysis — spatial proteomics, cell phenotyping, tumor-microenvironment characterization, immune profiling, and biomarker identification — across 20+ disease areas over harmonized datasets spanning 10M+ patients and 125M+ cells. The platform is delivered through a login-gated web application at app.enablemedicine.com; no public developer API is currently documented. Backed by initialized-capital, insight-partners, lightspeed-venture-partners, menlo-ventures, norwest-venture-partners, and sierra-ventures.

providers.name: Ferrum Health
providers.description: Ferrum Health is a healthcare AI governance company whose AI Governance Suite lets health systems deploy, validate, orchestrate, and monitor clinical AI models securely behind their own firewall, without protected health information leaving the health system. The vendor-neutral, privately deployed platform integrates once with existing EMR, PACS, and worklist infrastructure, then routes every clinical AI model — FDA-cleared, CE-marked, open-source, or homegrown — through a single secure path via its Deployment Fabric, curates 60+ applications in its Model Hub across radiology, cardiology, oncology, neurology, and musculoskeletal specialties, and continuously links predictions, ground truth, and outcomes for bias and drift detection through its Observability Lens. It is SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and GDPR aligned, and is used by Sutter Health, Carle Health, and 250+ sites.

providers.name: Flossy
providers.description: Flossy is a Santa Monica, California healthcare technology company that builds AI agents ("AI coworkers") for dental practices, veterinary clinics and med spas. Its named agents cover front-office and revenue-cycle work: Fiona handles inbound and outbound patient communication and scheduling across phone, SMS and web chat; Betsy scores call-center quality and marketing performance; Michael captures insurance, verifies benefits and surfaces billing insights; and Reid forecasts revenue and optimizes schedule capacity and staffing. FlossyHQ is the operator console the practice works in, and Agent Builder lets practices assemble custom agents. Founded in 2020 by Miles Beckett and Steve Seigel, Flossy began as a pay-as-you-go dental care marketplace and has since repositioned around agentic automation for practice operations. Flossy publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification; the one publicly reachable first-party integration surface is the embeddable Fiona web-chat widget.

providers.name: Foodsmart
providers.description: Foodsmart is a telenutrition company that pairs the nation's largest network of registered dietitians with a digital food-benefits platform, delivering personalized nutrition care via telehealth to more than three million members. The company partners with health plans and employers to reach Medicaid, Medicare, and commercial members, combining one-on-one dietitian counseling with meal planning, grocery ordering, and SNAP benefits enrollment. Foodsmart's "Foodscription" model connects clinical nutrition guidance to affordable, healthy food access to improve outcomes and lower the cost of diet-related chronic disease. This profile was surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Foodsmart exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Genome Medical
providers.description: Genome Medical is a telehealth-enabled genetic services provider offering expert genetic counseling, test selection and ordering support, results interpretation, and clinical trial matching for individuals with rare and hereditary conditions. It partners with health systems, life sciences organizations, and genetic testing labs to scale genetic care, reduce diagnostic backlogs, and accelerate diagnoses through a proprietary clinical platform and patient portal. Genome Medical does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Guidelight Health
providers.description: Guidelight Health is a mental healthcare provider delivering evidence-based day treatment programs — Partial Hospitalization Programs (PHPs) and Intensive Outpatient Programs (IOPs) — for people managing anxiety, depression, trauma, PTSD, and personality disorders. Care combines group therapy, individual psychotherapy, and medication management, offered in-person and virtually across Colorado, California, Massachusetts, North Carolina, and Washington. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), the company operates a patient-facing clinical service rather than a public developer API; its client portal runs on the third-party Kipu (kipuworks.com) EHR platform, so there is no first-party API, SDK, or developer surface to catalog at this time.

providers.name: Harmonycares
providers.description: HarmonyCares is a physician-led, value-based, in-home primary care organization headquartered in Troy, Michigan, and one of the nation's largest house-call practices. It brings primary care, palliative care, and ancillary services such as in-home laboratory, radiology, and comprehensive health assessments directly to older adults living with serious and complex chronic conditions. Operating across roughly a dozen states, HarmonyCares supports more than 70,000 patients through value-based arrangements with Medicare Advantage plans and Medicare ACO programs. The company was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a General Catalyst portfolio company; it publishes a public marketing site, a patient portal, and corporate policy documents, but no public developer program, API, or SDK was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Harris Ambulatory Care Enterprise
providers.description: Harris Ambulatory Care Enterprise (part of Harris Healthcare, a Harris Computer company) provides ambulatory healthcare software solutions including the Pulse electronic health record system. The platform supports a §170.315(g)(10) ONC certified FHIR API for third-party application developers to access patient data, provider information, and clinical resources. Pulse is deployed on-premises, so each provider hosts a separate API instance with its own base URL. Third-party developers must obtain an ONC 2015 Edition Certified API License and register with each provider organization.

providers.name: Inkblot Therapy
providers.description: Inkblot Therapy is a Canadian digital mental health platform, part of GreenShield, that delivers secure virtual therapy and counselling online. It matches individuals to licensed counsellors, social workers, psychotherapists, and psychologists using a clinically designed questionnaire, and delivers confidential video sessions. Inkblot serves individuals directly, employers and organizations through Employee Assistance Programs (EAP) and mental health benefits, and practitioners who provide care on the platform. The company operates consumer and business web applications (app.inkblottherapy.com, business.inkblottherapy.com) but does not publish a public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or an OpenAPI description. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; enrichment reflects the public web and DNS/security surface only.

providers.name: MiRus
providers.description: MiRus is a Marietta, Georgia life sciences company founded in 2015 that develops and commercializes implants and procedural solutions built on MoRe, its proprietary molybdenum-rhenium superalloy, for spine, orthopaedic and structural heart disease. Its FDA-cleared portfolio spans the Europa pedicle screw system, CYGNUS MoRe anterior cervical plating, 3DR printed interbody and corpectomy systems, the Atlas foot-and-ankle plating line, and the Siegel transcatheter aortic valve, alongside GALILEO — a spine-focused surgical planning, intra-operative alignment measurement and remote physiologic monitoring platform delivered to clinicians as the "Mirus Analytics" web application at rpm.mirusmed.com. MiRus publishes no public developer program: the GALILEO backend, which includes a FHIR route, is bearer/Cognito authenticated and answers 401 on every path, and no OpenAPI, SDK, reference or developer portal is published anywhere on its public surface.

providers.name: PB Health
providers.description: PB Health (PB Healthcare Service Pvt Ltd) is an India-based consumer healthcare network offering end-to-end care through a single app - online doctor consultations, hospital visits and admissions, lab tests and radiology scans, medicine ordering, diabetes and obesity management, preventive health packages, and structured home care and recovery. The platform spans top specialities including cardiology, gastroenterology, orthopaedics, pulmonology, internal medicine, gynaecology, ENT, paediatrics, and minimal-access and bariatric surgery, and helps families coordinate their complete health and insurance journey. PB Health is a consumer mobile application (iOS and Android) and website; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: PeopleOne Health
providers.description: PeopleOne Health is a nationwide provider of value-based, employer-funded advanced primary care, delivering comprehensive physical and mental health services with no copays, deductibles, or coinsurance for members. Its model pairs dedicated care teams with a prevention-first approach to lower total cost of care for self-funded employers while improving member health outcomes, and it was named a 2024 Best Nationwide Primary Care Provider by the Validation Institute. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV, PeopleOne Health operates as a healthcare services provider rather than an API platform: member access is delivered through a healow-based patient portal and a member portal, and no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer documentation is published.

providers.name: Phil
providers.description: PHIL (PHILRx) is a healthtech company operating a digital hub and direct-to-patient platform that helps pharmaceutical brands maximize prescription starts, insurance coverage, affordability, and medication adherence. Its all-in-one platform connects pharma manufacturers, patients, and healthcare providers to streamline the prescription access experience, run affordable direct-to-patient and cash-pay programs, and improve commercial performance across the medication access journey. PHIL is a portfolio company of Uncork Capital. As of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Plenna
providers.description: Plenna is a women's healthcare provider operating a network of integrated medical clinics across Mexico City, redefining health for women across every life stage. Its services span gynecology, maternity and prenatal care, fertility, menopause, contraception, gynecological surgery, psychology, nutrition, laboratory studies, vaccines and lactation support, delivered across six physical clinics (Tlalpan, Coapa, Del Valle, Polanco, San Angel and Satelite) and through Portal Plenna, a patient portal and iOS/Android mobile app for scheduling appointments, virtual consultations, test results, prescriptions and pregnancy tracking. Plenna is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Radish Health
providers.description: Radish Health is a healthcare company that provides employers with a modern employee health benefit, pairing each member with a dedicated care team and physicians who handle medical issues directly or coordinate specialist referrals. The service emphasizes direct-access primary care over phone, video, and in-person visits, with rapid response times and appointment coordination aimed at reducing employer healthcare costs while improving the patient experience. Radish Health is delivered through patient-facing web and mobile apps (iOS and Android) and an employer benefits program; it is a Techstars portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass, Radish Health publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation — this profile captures its identity, legal/support surfaces, and domain security posture only.

providers.name: Rezilient Health
providers.description: Rezilient Health is an employer-sponsored primary and specialty care provider that combines physical CloudClinics with telehealth to deliver unlimited, zero-cost care to employees on behalf of employers, health plans, health systems, and brokers. Its hybrid CloudClinic model pairs on-site medical staff with remote physicians and connected diagnostic equipment so members can access in-person and virtual visits, with the goal of lowering total healthcare spend and improving clinical outcomes. Rezilient offers patient-facing web and mobile apps for scheduling and care, but publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the honest result is that Rezilient operates a consumer/enterprise healthcare service rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: Season Health
providers.description: Season Health is a food-as-medicine platform that helps people living with chronic conditions eat well and live well. It connects patients with registered dietitians, personalized nutrition and meal plans, and medically-tailored groceries and meals, and works with health plans and care providers to deliver nutrition care as a covered benefit. The consumer and provider experiences run through app.seasonhealth.com; the company is a HIPAA-covered digital health service. Season Health is backed by a16z. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs — api.seasonhealth.com is a private application backend — so this profile captures the company's real public web properties rather than an API program.

providers.name: Sira Medical
providers.description: Sira Medical develops augmented reality software that transforms 3D radiological imaging into patient-specific holographic models projected onto real-world backgrounds. Delivered through head-mounted AR devices (such as Microsoft HoloLens) and mobile platforms, the technology helps surgeons perform preoperative planning with greater confidence, clinicians educate patients with understandable visualizations, medical schools train students on patient-specific anatomy, and medical-device makers design and validate implants. The company is backed by 500 Global, Eileses Capital, UCSF Innovation Ventures, and Microsoft for Startups. Sira Medical operates as a clinical AR software vendor and does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity, legal, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Verisian
providers.description: Verisian is an AI infrastructure platform for clinical trials, giving pharmaceutical sponsors and CROs the information infrastructure required to deploy AI across their experts and processes. The platform provides full study traceability and automates statistical programming workflows: automating the validation of SDTM and ADaM analysis datasets (turning time-consuming QC double-programming into value-generating QA oversight), and generating complete define-XML files and draft reviewer's guides that are guaranteed consistent with the underlying analysis, so teams are submission-ready in hours. Verisian is cloud native, compatible with any statistical computing environment (SCE), storage, or compute, and integrates through simple file transfer with no complex API integration required. It serves statistical programmers, statisticians, data managers, medical writers, clinicians, and regulatory teams across in-house and CRO-outsourced operating models; Bayer is a named customer. There is no public developer API surface — the product is an enterprise application (app.verisian.com) accessed after sales onboarding.

providers.name: VetSource
providers.description: VetSource is a veterinary technology and pharmacy company founded in 2008 that delivers a suite of pharmacy, technology, and business services for the pet health industry. Its offerings span home-delivery prescription management (an online pharmacy and prescription workflow that lets veterinary practices prescribe and fulfill medications with compliance and revenue tools), the Vet2Pet client-engagement platform (a custom-branded app connecting practices with pet owners for communication, reminders, loyalty, and telehealth), and data/analytics services that provide industry benchmarking and practice performance insights. VetSource serves veterinary practices and pet owners across North America. No public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation is published; this profile captures the company identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Briya
providers.description: Briya builds AIRE (AI Research Environment), a privacy-first AI platform for healthcare and clinical research that lets researchers analyze real-world medical data without writing code. AIRE trains AI models on real-world data and provides domain-specific agents for literature review, hypothesis testing, population and cohort analysis, study design, and manuscript-ready output with built-in validation. Data is accessed across multiple sources without centralizing it into a warehouse, with a compliance posture aimed at HIPAA, GDPR, and FDA/EMA regulatory standards. Briya serves emerging biotech, life sciences organizations, academic institutions, and healthcare systems, with offices in New York, Nashville, and Tel Aviv. The company is backed by Insight Partners. This API Evangelist profile is an enrichment pass on a portfolio lead; Briya publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Cytovale
providers.description: Cytovale is a San Francisco-based medical diagnostics company that develops early-detection technology for sepsis. Its flagship product, IntelliSep, is the first and only FDA-cleared in vitro diagnostic test for sepsis: it uses microfluidics, high-speed video, and computer-vision algorithms to measure the biophysical rigidity of tens of thousands of white blood cells, detecting the immune activation that signals sepsis risk and returning a risk stratification in roughly eight minutes. The test runs on the Cytovale System medical device in emergency-department settings. Cytovale is venture-backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Sands Capital, and the Global Health Investment Corporation. The company operates as a clinical/diagnostics device maker and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Medix Infusion
providers.description: Medix Infusion, Inc. is a technology-enabled infusion care provider headquartered in Addison, Texas, that administers infusion and injectable therapies — anti-infectives, biologics, IVIG and other specialty medications — to chronically and acutely ill patients through a network of ambulatory infusion suites and in the home. The company concentrates on rural, suburban and other under-served markets, coordinating benefits investigation, prior authorization, scheduling, pharmacy and nursing around each referral, and is accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Health Care (ACHC). It raised a $35M Series B led by Echo Health Ventures in January 2023 alongside existing investor Noro-Moseley Partners. Medix Infusion operates as a care-delivery organization: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract on any public host as of this profile.

providers.name: Parallel Learning
providers.description: Parallel Learning is a special education services and staffing platform that connects K-12 schools and districts with a nationwide network of licensed clinicians for the remote delivery of specialized student support. Through its proprietary, HIPAA/FERPA-compliant Pathway platform it delivers virtual psychoeducational and neurodevelopmental assessments, speech-language therapy, behavioral and mental-health counseling, specialized instruction in reading, writing, and math, and executive-function coaching, pairing secure teletherapy with progress tracking and clinical oversight so districts can meet compliance requirements and improve student outcomes. The company serves thousands of students across dozens of states and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Pivotal Health
providers.description: Pivotal Health (formerly Radix Health) is a healthcare technology company and self-described "IDR Authority" that helps medical providers secure fair out-of-network reimbursement through the federal Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process created by the No Surprises Act. Its platform combines automated eligibility screening, dispute submission software integrated with major revenue cycle management (RCM) systems, payer data, and white-glove managed services across emergency medicine, anesthesiology, radiology, surgery, pathology, air ambulance, and hospitals and health systems. Pivotal Health is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: River Health
providers.description: River Health is an employer-sponsored virtual-first health plan operated by Mountain (joinmountain.com) that gives employees comprehensive primary and behavioral care at no cost to them. Members get unlimited virtual primary care and in-person doctor visits, behavioral health and therapy, thousands of free medications with home delivery or pharmacy pickup, free preventive care and screenings, after-hours urgent care, no-cost specialty and chronic- condition care, and free lab testing through Quest Diagnostics. Employers from small businesses to the Fortune 500 sponsor the plan; members enroll and manage care through the River Health member app at app.helloriver.com. River Health is a portfolio company of Techstars. No public developer API, documentation, or developer portal has been published.

providers.name: Ruma Care
providers.description: Ruma Care is a healthcare software company that streamlines the prior authorization process for biologic and infusion medications in infusion clinics. Its AI-powered platform pulls patient and insurance data from electronic health records (EHRs) to identify payer requirements, auto-populates payer-specific prior authorization forms with clinical data, flags missing documentation, and then manages insurer communication and follow-up until an authorization is approved. Built by former infusion clinic staff, Ruma Care consolidates the manual portal, fax, and paper workflows behind buy-and-bill and infusion services into a single platform to reduce denials and accelerate patient access to biologics. Ruma Care is a Y Combinator-backed company. As of this profile the company exposes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Simplifeye
providers.description: Simplifeye is a dental practice management platform that helps practices grow and streamline front-office operations through integrated payments, online scheduling, live webchat, and patient-engagement campaigns. Its HIPAA-compliant payments product supports in-office transactions, invoicing, and customizable payment plans; its 24/7 real-time online scheduler lets patients self-book appointments; and its live webchat is staffed by real people who answer patient questions and qualify leads outside business hours. Simplifeye was acquired by Vyne Dental and integrates with the Vyne Trellis billing platform for claims, eligibility, and revenue acceleration. Simplifeye operates a private, authenticated backend (api.simplifeye.co) that powers its dashboard and patient-facing widgets, but publishes no public developer program, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Viz.ai
providers.description: Viz.ai is a healthcare AI company that builds an intelligent care coordination platform. Its FDA-cleared, AI-powered software analyzes medical imaging (CT, CTA, MRI, echocardiography) to detect suspected disease — stroke (large vessel occlusion, ICH), aneurysm, pulmonary embolism, and cardiovascular conditions — and automatically alerts and connects the multidisciplinary care team in real time to accelerate diagnosis and treatment. Backed by CRV, GV, Insight Partners, Scale Venture Partners, Seedcamp, Susa Ventures, and Threshold Ventures. Viz.ai exposes no public developer API; integration is delivered through clinical/enterprise deployment, and its governance-relevant public surface is a Drata-hosted Trust Center documenting a broad security and compliance program (SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, and an extensive ISO family including ISO 42001 for AI management).

providers.name: Alvee Health
providers.description: Alvee Health is an AI-powered care navigation platform for social determinants of health (SDOH) and whole-person care coordination. It surfaces unmet social and clinical needs from documentation, auto-codes Z-codes, automates patient outreach and benefits enrollment through an autonomous care navigator, generates compliant billing documentation, and tracks outcomes so providers can capture reimbursement for CHI, PIN, CCM, PCM, and G0136 care-coordination codes. The platform is HIPAA compliant and SMART on FHIR certified, integrating with EHRs to embed social drivers of health into clinical workflows. Alvee is a Techstars Iowa (2022) portfolio company.

providers.name: Health Scholars
providers.description: Health Scholars — which rebranded to UpSkillAI in 2025 and now trades at upskillai.com — builds AI-powered extended reality (XR/VR) simulation training for mission-critical, hands-on work in healthcare, emergency medical services, stroke assessment and defense. The platform pairs voice-driven VR simulations with simulation management and readiness reporting, letting hospital systems, first responders and government programs run standardized protocol training on headsets without instructors or extra equipment. Customers reach it through a hosted web console at app.upskillai.com. The company publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, SDK, webhook catalog or public pricing. The production backend behind its own application (api.upskillai.com, with the legacy AWS API Gateway host api.healthscholars.com) is private and rejects unauthenticated requests.

providers.name: Juxta
providers.description: Juxta is a San Francisco positioning-technology company building a hardware-free Universal Positioning System (UPS) that delivers real-time indoor and outdoor tracking for people, assets, and robots with sub-meter accuracy indoors and roughly 3-meter accuracy outdoors. Rather than relying on satellites, beacons, or cameras, Juxta uses the inertial (IMU) sensors already present in mobile devices, robots, and machinery combined with machine-learning "synthetic fingerprinting" to map and track subjects in GPS-denied environments such as warehouses, hospitals, underground facilities, and battlefields. Its drag-and-drop deployment ingests a floorplan, satellite image, or CAD file and goes live in hours, priced by mapped area and assets tracked. Juxta serves defense, logistics and robotics, and healthcare, and is backed by Y Combinator and other early-stage investors. Access today is through a partner portal and booked demo; no public developer API is documented.

providers.name: Modern Animal
providers.description: Modern Animal is a membership-based veterinary healthcare company operating physical primary and urgent care clinics across major U.S. metropolitan regions, combining in-clinic visits with 24/7 virtual veterinary consultations, pharmacy and prescription management, dental care, surgery, and preventive care. It runs a subscription membership model (All Access, Essential, and Pay As You Go tiers) with transparent, upfront pricing and a companion mobile app for booking and virtual care. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and susa-ventures. Modern Animal is a consumer veterinary brand and publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Oshi Health
providers.description: Oshi Health is a virtual, whole-person gastrointestinal (GI) care clinic delivering insurance-covered telehealth to patients with digestive conditions such as IBS, GERD, Crohn's disease, and ulcerative colitis. Care is provided by a coordinated team of GI providers, registered dietitians, and gut-brain behavioral health specialists, and is offered to members through major health plans and employers. Oshi Health is a patient-facing healthcare services company rather than an API producer; it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or /.well-known/ discovery surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and enriched with the artifacts the company genuinely publishes.

providers.name: ABILITY Network (Inovalon)
providers.description: ABILITY Network is a healthcare SaaS business acquired by Inovalon in 2018 and now delivered as part of the cloud-based Inovalon ONE Platform. It provides US healthcare providers with software for medical billing and claims management, eligibility verification, revenue cycle management, clinical quality reporting, patient access, and workforce/staffing and care coordination. Inovalon pairs these provider-facing applications with large national datasets and analytics to support data-driven healthcare across payers, providers, pharmacies, and life-sciences organizations. Developer access to Inovalon ONE APIs is offered through the authenticated Inovalon developer portal at developer.inovalonone.com, which exposes sandbox, staging, and live environments.

providers.name: Alto Pharmacy
providers.description: Alto Pharmacy is a San Francisco-based digital pharmacy and pharmacy-technology company (founded 2015 as ScriptDash) that combines a full-service licensed pharmacy with a proprietary pharmacy operating system, Alto OS. Alto fills retail, specialty and fertility prescriptions with same-day courier delivery, pharmacist care and automated benefits investigation, and it sells that stack to industry partners as Alto Hub+, Alto Dispensing and Alto Complete — hub services, dispensing and end-to-end pharmacy-as-a-service for pharmaceutical manufacturers, health plans, health systems and digital health companies. Alto markets intake, transfer and Surescripts-based integrations to those partners, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable specification; technical access runs through its partnerships team.

providers.name: Capstan Medical
providers.description: Capstan Medical is a Santa Cruz, California medical device company founded in 2020 out of the Occam Labs incubator by Dan Wallace, with Maggie Nixon as CEO. The company is developing a surgical robotics platform for structural heart disease, merging robotic catheter navigation with next-generation transcatheter mitral and tricuspid valve implants so heart valves can be repaired or replaced without open heart surgery. In 2025 Capstan completed what it describes as the world's first robotic catheter mitral valve replacements in humans, and it raised a $110M Series C led by Eclipse with participation from Intuitive Ventures and Yu Galaxy, bringing total funding past $150M ahead of a second-generation system planned for 2026. Capstan is pre-commercial and regulated medical device focused: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contracts.

providers.name: Click Therapeutics
providers.description: Click Therapeutics, Inc. is a New York-headquartered digital medicine company founded in 2012 by David Benshoof Klein that develops, validates, and commercializes software as prescription medical treatments — the category it named Digital Therapeutics. Its AI-enabled platform targets diseases with an underlying neurological or behavioral component through cognitive and neurobehavioral mechanisms, delivered as smartphone software used independently or alongside biomedical therapy (Software-Enhanced Drugs). Authorized and commercial programs include CT-152 (Rejoyn, major depressive disorder, developed with Otsuka), CT-132 (episodic migraine) and AspyreRx (type 2 diabetes), with a pipeline spanning schizophrenia (CT-155 with Boehringer Ingelheim, CT-156), opioid use disorder, multiple sclerosis, atopic dermatitis, obesity, oncology, insomnia and acute coronary syndrome. Click publishes no public developer program, API, or SDK — its software is distributed as regulated prescription therapeutics, not as a platform.

providers.name: Healthera
providers.description: Healthera is a United Kingdom digital-health and patient-engagement company, founded in 2015 by Cambridge University students and headquartered in Cambridge, England. It runs a patient-facing pharmacy app and website for ordering NHS prescriptions and medicines online and booking pharmacy services (Pharmacy First, treatments, vaccinations), alongside a pharmacy-facing SaaS "Patient Experience Platform" used by 1,700+ community pharmacies to manage repeat prescriptions, bookings, marketing, and delivery. In November 2022 Healthera became the first pharmacy app to integrate with the NHS Electronic Prescription Service (EPS), and it connects to NHS Digital / NHS England systems plus third-party platforms such as myGP, eConsult, Cegedim Rx Pharmacy Manager, Medpoint, Royal Mail, and Uber for same-hour delivery. Healthera markets custom integration APIs to pharmacy and brand partners, but as of this review it publishes no public developer portal, no self-serve API documentation, and no machine-readable contract; its api.healthera.co.uk "Healthera Core" host is a private backend and exposes no FHIR CapabilityStatement. Integration is partner-gated rather than self-serve.

providers.name: Nalu Medical
providers.description: Nalu Medical, Inc. is a privately held, commercial-stage medical device company headquartered in Carlsbad, California, that develops the Nalu Neurostimulation System for the management of chronic pain. The system pairs a battery-free micro implantable pulse generator (mIPG) with an externally worn Therapy Disc that powers it wirelessly, and is controlled by the patient through a smartphone-based remote-control application; it is FDA-cleared for both spinal cord stimulation (SCS) and peripheral nerve stimulation (PNS). Nalu publishes patient and provider resources, instructions for use, clinical evidence and peer-reviewed publications on nalumed.com. It operates no public developer program - as of the 2026-08-26 enrichment pass there is no API reference, no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, no SDK, no MCP server and no developer portal on any host the company controls.

providers.name: Paradromics
providers.description: Paradromics is a clinical-stage neurotechnology company headquartered in Austin, Texas, with a machine-learning and data-science office in Oakland, California, developing high-data-rate implantable brain-computer interfaces (BCI). Founded in 2019 by Matt Angle, the company builds the Connexus BCI, an investigational fully implantable system that records high-resolution intracortical neural activity and transmits it through the skin to an external system that decodes intended speech, text and digital device control for people with severe motor impairment. Connexus holds FDA Breakthrough Device Designations for speech decoding (2023) and digital device control (2024), was accepted into the FDA Total Product Life Cycle Advisory Program, and received an Investigational Device Exemption in November 2025 for the Connect-One Early Feasibility Study (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07357428). Tempo BCI is a pre-clinical-trial pipeline product. Paradromics publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract; its only machine-readable public surface is an llms.txt AI-context file at paradromics.com/llms.txt.

providers.name: Pi Health
providers.description: Pi Health is an AI-native clinical trial technology company and contract research organization (CRO) building FICS, a unified operating system for oncology and global clinical trials. Its platform consolidates traditionally fragmented systems — Electronic Data Capture (EDC), Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS), electronic Trial Master File (eTMF), electronic Investigator Site File (eISF), and an EMR-to-EDC Orchestrator — into a single AI-validated master record spanning study startup through closeout. Pi Health pairs the platform with CRO services and a global research network with oncology sites across the US, Brazil, Australia, and India. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this remains an identity profile in the API Evangelist network awaiting a public API.

providers.name: Smile Digital Health
providers.description: Smile Digital Health (formerly Smile CDR) is a Toronto-based health interoperability software company and the commercial steward of the open source HAPI FHIR project (the world's most widely deployed Java implementation of the HL7 FHIR standard). Its flagship product, Smile CDR — marketed under the broader Smile Omni portfolio as the OmniVera Health Data Platform — is a FHIR-native clinical data repository and integration platform that ingests HL7 v2.x, CDA, CSV, JSON, XML, and FHIR payloads, normalizes them into FHIR (R4, R5, STU3, DSTU2), and exposes them through a hardened FHIR REST API, SMART on FHIR / OAuth2 / OIDC security, Bulk Data export, Subscriptions, MDM, Terminology Services, CQL-based Quality Measures, and a JSON Admin API. The platform is deployed on-prem and across AWS, Azure, and GCP, with HITRUST v9.4, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and ONC 2015 Edition certifications, and is used by 190+ global customers, including 30+ US payers running CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization (CMS-0057-F) workloads on its CMS Suite. Adjacent Smile Omni product families include OmniCompli (regulatory compliance, including CMS Suite and CMS Concierge), OmniQ (digital quality measures / HEDIS, Intelligence Hub), and OmniConcierge (managed and professional services). The primary developer surface is the FHIR REST API, with per-endpoint auto-generated OpenAPI / Swagger UI at `{baseUrl}/swagger-ui/`, plus a separate JSON Admin API for cluster, module, user, audit, batch job, MDM, and OpenID Connect administration.

providers.name: Synyi
providers.description: Synyi (森亿智能 / Shanghai Synyi Medical Technology Co., Ltd.) is a Shanghai-based medical artificial-intelligence company founded in April 2016 that builds AI and big-data systems for hospitals. Its platform uses medical natural-language processing, large-scale medical knowledge graphs and multi-agent LLM applications to normalize and mine the unstructured clinical records held in Chinese hospital information systems, and sells that capability as deployed hospital software spanning clinical decision support, medical-record quality control, hospital operations management, an AI-driven clinic model and clinical research tooling. IDC's "China Healthcare Big Data Solution Market Share, 2023" ranked Synyi first in its market. Synyi publishes no public API, no developer portal and no machine-readable contract; its products are enterprise systems deployed inside customer hospitals and reached through a direct sales motion.

providers.name: Unlearn
providers.description: Unlearn is a San Francisco AI company that builds digital twin generators for clinical trials — machine learning models trained on patient-level historical data that forecast an individual participant's clinical outcomes under control or standard of care. Sponsors use these AI-generated digital twins to plan trials, monitor clinical data, and run smaller, more powerful studies; the approach is qualified by the EMA and aligned with current FDA guidance. Unlearn is backed by 8VC and DCVC and publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Curative
providers.description: Curative is a health insurance and healthcare services company founded in 2020 that reengineered the employer-based health plan around simplicity, engagement, and cost transparency. Its fully insured and level-funded plans give members a competitive monthly premium with zero copays, deductibles, or out-of-pocket costs, starting each member with a baseline visit that tailors a preventative care plan. Curative serves more than 1,200 employer clients and over 165,000 members, reached profitability, and achieved unicorn status ($1.275B valuation) following a $150M Series B round backed by DCVC. Curative operates as a HIPAA-regulated health plan; it has no public developer/API program, so this API Evangelist profile captures company identity, its member/provider web surface, and probed domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: DXY
providers.description: DXY (丁香园) is China's leading digital healthcare technology company, founded in 2000 in Harbin and headquartered in Hangzhou. It operates a "D+C" dual strategy: a professional physician community and clinical toolset (drug reference "用药助手", clinical case database, medical education, and the "Insight" pharmaceutical data analytics platform) alongside consumer health services under the "丁香医生" (Dingxiang Doctor) brand. DXY also runs the Biomart / 丁香通 life-sciences supplies marketplace. Its Medical Data Open Platform (open.dxy.cn) exposes standardized healthcare data services — newly-approved drugs, drug SKU and drug search, disease search, and hospital/institution search — as REST/JSON APIs under api.dxy.cn for pharmaceutical, medical, and health-tech partners. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Intus Care
providers.description: IntusCare (Intus Care, Inc.) is a Providence, Rhode Island health technology company building an end-to-end software and services ecosystem for PACE — Programs of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly. Founded in 2019 by Brown University students Robbie Felton, Evan Jackson and Alex Rothberg, it launched population health analytics at PACE of Rhode Island in 2020 and now serves 70+ PACE organizations. Its products are CareHub, a PACE-native ONC-certified EMR and care-management platform; IRIS, a risk-adjustment and coding system for PACE and value-based care organizations; and a Population Health & Utilization Management suite delivered with fractionally-staffed Integrated Care Services clinicians. IntusCare markets interoperability and out-of-the-box third-party administrator (TPA) integrations, but as of this profile it publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable contract — customer-facing surfaces are the authenticated CareHub and analytics applications.

providers.name: SnapCare
providers.description: SnapCare is an Atlanta-based healthcare workforce company, founded in 2017 as SnapNurse and relaunched under the SnapCare name in 2023, that pairs a national clinician marketplace with Booker, its SaaS workforce platform for hospitals, post-acute facilities, agency suppliers and clinicians. Booker combines predictive scheduling against census and historical demand trends, real-time per-diem shift fulfillment, internal float-pool management, same-day pay, and escalation of unfilled shifts to approved contingent suppliers. SnapCare acquired predictive staffing analytics vendor Medecipher in 2024 and merged with the nurse community connectRN in April 2026, raising a Series A led by Suvretta Capital. SnapCare sells the platform to healthcare organizations rather than to developers; no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API contract was found on its public surface.

providers.name: Accolade
providers.description: Accolade is a personalized healthcare and benefits navigation platform for employers and health plans. It pairs members with a care team of advocates, registered nurses, physicians, and mental-health specialists to help them understand their benefits, find in-network care, book appointments, and manage chronic and complex conditions. Accolade combines this human advocacy with virtual primary care, expert medical opinion, and mental-health services delivered through its member web and mobile apps. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. Accolade is a member-facing benefits platform and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Baba
providers.description: Baba Care, Inc. is a healthcare company that provides patient advocacy and care-navigation services for Medicare beneficiaries in the United States. Operating under the tagline "Healthcare simplified," Baba pairs each member with a dedicated advocate who handles their healthcare headaches — coordinating care, benefits, and administrative tasks — with the service covered by Medicare. The member experience is delivered through a login-gated web application at baba.care; the company publishes no public developer or API surface at this time. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Finni Health
providers.description: Finni Health is a telehealth company that connects families of children on the autism spectrum with Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) therapists and mental health providers. Operating across more than 30 states, Finni offers both in-home and in-clinic ABA therapy with flexible scheduling, handles insurance coordination and billing for its provider network, and gives parents a portal for progress tracking and family-led goal setting. The company positions itself as an operating platform for ABA practices as well as a care provider for families, but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API specifications at this time.

providers.name: Medely
providers.description: Medely is a healthcare workforce orchestration platform and staffing marketplace that connects healthcare facilities with a network of qualified nurses and allied health professionals. What began as a marketplace to match facilities with per-diem talent has grown into a full workforce management platform, helping hospitals, surgery centers, skilled nursing facilities, and other providers fill open and per-diem shifts, support their core clinical teams, and maintain high-quality patient care. Medely offers credentialing, scheduling, and flexible workforce management tools, and holds the Joint Commission's Gold Seal of Approval for its staffing services. The company is backed by General Catalyst and Wing Venture Capital. Medely does not currently operate a public developer program or documented API; its GraphQL backend at api.medely.com powers the first-party web and mobile applications only.

providers.name: Provide
providers.description: Provide is a financial services division of Fifth Third Bank offering banking and financing built specifically for owners of professional practices — dental, medical, veterinary, optometry, childcare, financial advisory, funeral, and insurance businesses. The company provides conventional and SBA loans to start, acquire, or expand a practice, alongside a full suite of customized banking products. Provide was acquired by Fifth Third Bank and operates as a specialty lending and banking brand. Surfaced as a portfolio company of QED Investors; it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Standard Practice
providers.description: Standard Practice builds voice AI for healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM) teams. Its AI agents place and handle outbound phone calls to insurance payers to automate administrative work — claim status follow-up, benefits verification, prior authorization, and EDI enrollment — so billing teams can scale collections and get paid more, faster. The platform is delivered as a private, login-gated web application. The company was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and Wing Venture Capital and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: Bamboo Health
providers.description: Bamboo Health (formerly Appriss Health + PatientPing) is a healthcare technology company delivering Real-Time Care Intelligence across the physical and behavioral health continuum. It operates one of the nation's largest care-collaboration networks, connecting health systems, health plans, pharmacies, and state agencies through prescription drug monitoring (PDMP), care coordination, and behavioral healthcare navigation. Flagship solutions include Bamboo Bridge, OpenBeds, Pings, NarxCare, and the PMP AWARxE state monitoring platform. Backed by Insight Partners, the company supports over a billion patient encounters annually. Bamboo Health does not publish a public developer API; integrations are delivered through EHR workflows and partner/state programs. Security posture is documented in a public Trust Center (SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST CSF, HIPAA, NIST 800-53).

providers.name: Biofourmis
providers.description: Biofourmis is a health technology company founded in 2015, with offices in Boston, Singapore and India, that partners with health systems, hospitals, payers and life science companies to deliver care in the home. Its platform combines medical-grade device connectivity, FDA-cleared algorithms and digital biomarkers, a patient mobile app and clinician dashboard, and 70+ dynamic care pathways to support Hospital at Home, Timely Discharge, SNF at Home and Remote Patient Monitoring programs. Biofourmis merged with CopilotIQ in October 2024 to form an end-to-end platform for AI-driven in-home care; ActiGraph acquired the Biofourmis life science business in January 2025. The company markets EMR integration and device-agnostic connectivity to enterprise healthcare customers, but publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Cagent Vascular
providers.description: Cagent Vascular is a privately held endovascular medical device company based in Wayne, Pennsylvania, that develops and commercializes Serration Remodeling Therapy (SRT). Its flagship product, the Serranator PTA Serration Balloon Catheter, embeds stainless-steel serrated strips into a semi-compliant angioplasty balloon to create linear, interrupted micro-fissures along the artery wall, producing controlled lumen expansion at lower pressures when treating peripheral artery disease (PAD) and chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). The Serranator is FDA 510(k) cleared and CE marked, and the portfolio has expanded to include Serranator SL-PRO and the Serranator SONIC intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) system. Cagent Vascular is a device manufacturer rather than a software or platform company: it publishes clinical data, case studies, webinars and reimbursement material on its website, but no public developer program, API, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Clarapath
providers.description: Clarapath is a medical robotics company headquartered in Hawthorne, New York that automates the tissue sectioning step of the clinical histopathology workflow. Its FDA-registered SectionStar platform pairs patented tape-transfer sectioning with precision robotics, integrated optics and sensors, and computational quality control to turn paraffin blocks into standardized slides with quantitative quality metrics. The company also ships the TrimStar Pro trimming system, a HistoStation data repository for sample and image traceability, remote Telehistology operation, and histology consulting services for hospital, reference, and veterinary laboratories.

providers.name: Digital Diagnostics
providers.description: Digital Diagnostics is a healthcare AI company based in Coralville, Iowa, founded by Dr. Michael Abramoff. It builds autonomous artificial-intelligence diagnostic systems that make a medical diagnosis at the point of care without requiring a physician to interpret the result. Its flagship product, LumineticsCore (formerly IDx-DR), was the first FDA-cleared autonomous AI diagnostic system and detects diabetic retinopathy from fundus images in about 30 seconds, reimbursed under CPT code 92229 and integrated with EHR systems such as Epic. A companion product, SphereDx, provides securely hosted diagnostic result management. The company is a portfolio company of 8vc and is researching additional indications including glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration, cardiovascular, and neurodegenerative disease detection via retinal imaging. Digital Diagnostics emphasizes ethical, equitable AI ("AI the right way") and holds ISO 13485:2016 quality-management certification. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Galvanize Therapeutics
providers.description: Galvanize Therapeutics, Inc. is a Redwood City, California medical device company founded in 2015 by Jonathan Waldstreicher, MD and William Krimsky, MD, and created and incubated by Apple Tree Partners (ATP). Galvanize develops pulsed electric field (PEF) therapies that deliver high-voltage, short-duration energy locally to alter the transmembrane potential of targeted cells, inducing non-thermal regulated cell death without denaturing cellular proteins or the extracellular matrix. Its Aliya PEF System is cleared for surgical ablation of soft tissue and is being studied in non-small cell lung cancer, while RheOx addresses chronic bronchitis in the airway. The company received FDA 510(k) clearance for the Aliya EX Generator in May 2026. Galvanize is a privately held, clinically-focused device manufacturer and publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Halo Health (Symplr)
providers.description: Halo Health, now part of symplr and marketed as symplr Clinical Communications, is a HIPAA-compliant clinical communication and collaboration platform for healthcare organizations. It provides role-based secure messaging, voice communication, critical alert and clinical-alarm notification, and on-call schedule management so care teams can coordinate around patients. The platform integrates with hospital EHR and clinical systems using healthcare interoperability standards - HL7 ADT for patient admit/discharge/transfer events, HL7 ORU for laboratory and radiology results, and SMTP for alerts such as sepsis notifications - rather than through a documented public developer REST API. symplr acquired Halo Health to extend its healthcare operations software portfolio, and the product now sits alongside symplr's broader workforce, compliance, and provider-data solutions.

providers.name: HD
providers.description: HD is an AI-native healthcare marketplace and patient-navigation platform for emerging Southeast Asia, headquartered in Bangkok, Thailand. Its consumer surface, HDmall, is a health, dental, aesthetics, and surgery marketplace that lets patients compare transparent pricing and book online across 30,000+ services from 3,000+ clinics and hospitals in Thailand (hdmall.co.th) and Indonesia (hdmall.id). AI-powered navigation turns patient symptoms into personalized, safety-checked care recommendations, and HDcare adds human-led, AI-assisted concierge support for complex surgical cases. The platform has navigated over 500,000 patients. HD is a consumer-facing healthtech operator with no public developer API or portal; the strongest machine-readable surface it publishes today is an llms.txt guiding LLMs to its canonical content. HD is a portfolio company of Partech, added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment tracking.

providers.name: Imbria Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Imbria Pharmaceuticals is a private, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in the Boston area that is developing novel cardiovascular therapies targeting cardiac energy metabolism. Its lead candidate, ninerafaxstat, is a first-in-class partial fatty acid oxidation (pFOX) inhibitor designed to shift myocardial substrate utilization toward glucose oxidation, generating more ATP per unit of oxygen consumed and improving cardiac metabolic efficiency without affecting heart rate, rhythm, ejection fraction or blood pressure. Ninerafaxstat is in the global FORTITUDE-HCM Phase 2b trial (NCT07023614) for symptomatic non-obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (nHCM), which has no approved treatments, and holds FDA Orphan Drug Designation for that indication; a Phase 2b in cardiometabolic HFpEF is planned. The company is backed by RA Capital, SV Health Investors, Deep Track Capital, Catalio Capital Management, AN Ventures and Cytokinetics.
